title.zh: 卷三百九十三 列傳第一百五十二 彭龜年 黃裳 羅點 黃度 周南 林大中 陳騤 黃黼 詹體仁
title.en: Volume 393 Biographies 152: Peng Guinian, Huang Chang, Luo Dian, Huang Du, Zhou Nan, Lin Dazhong, Chen Kui, Huang Fu, Zhan Tiren
title.raw: 卷三百九十三 列傳第一百五十二 彭龜年 黃裳 羅點 黃度 周南 林大中 陳騤 黃黼 詹體仁 Volume 393 Biographies 152: Peng Guinian, Huang Chang, Luo Dian, Huang Du, Zhou Nan, Lin Dazhong, Chen Kui, Huang Fu, Zhan Tiren

sentences.zh: 彭龜年

translations.literal: Peng Guinian
translations.idiomatic: Peng Guinian

sentences.zh: 彭龜年，字子壽，臨江軍清江人。

translations.literal: Peng Guinian, courtesy name Zishou, was a native of Qingjiang in Linjiang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Guinian, styled Zishou, came from Qingjiang in Linjiang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 七歲而孤，事母盡孝。

translations.literal: At age seven he was orphaned and served his mother with utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned at seven, he devoted himself to his mother with exemplary filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 性穎異，讀書能解大義。

translations.literal: His nature was exceptionally keen; in reading he could grasp the larger meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Gifted by nature, he read for the larger meaning rather than mere words.

sentences.zh: 及長，得程氏《易》讀之，至忘寢食，從朱熹、張栻質疑，而學益明。

translations.literal: When grown, he obtained the Cheng family's Book of Changes and read it until he forgot sleep and food; he questioned Zhu Xi and Zhang Shi to resolve doubts, and his learning grew ever clearer.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he acquired the Cheng school edition of the Book of Changes and studied it until he neglected sleep and meals; he sought clarification from Zhu Xi and Zhang Shi, and his understanding deepened accordingly.

sentences.zh: 登乾道五年進士第，授袁州宜春尉、吉州安福丞。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Qiandao he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed registrar of Yichun in Yuan Prefecture and assistant magistrate of Anfu in Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He placed on the jinshi roll in Qiandao 5 (1169) and was posted as registrar of Yichun in Yuan Prefecture and assistant magistrate of Anfu in Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 鄭僑、張枃同薦，除太學博士。

translations.literal: Zheng Qiao and Zhang Shi jointly recommended him, and he was appointed erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: On joint recommendation by Zheng Qiao and Zhang Shi, he was made a doctorate lecturer at the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 殿中侍御史劉光祖以論帶御器械吳端，徙太府少卿，龜年上疏乞復其位，貽書宰相云：「祖宗嘗改易差除以伸臺諫之氣，不聞改易臺諫以伸幸臣之私。」

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Censor Liu Guangzu, for criticizing Wu Duan, bearer of the imperial arms, was transferred to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Supplies. Guinian memorialized requesting restoration of his post and wrote to the chief ministers, saying: "The ancestral emperors sometimes altered appointments and dismissals to assert the spirit of the censorate and remonstrance officials; one never hears of altering censorate and remonstrance officials to indulge the private interests of favored ministers."
translations.idiomatic: When Palace Attendant Censor Liu Guangzu was demoted to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Supplies for criticizing Wu Duan, bearer of the imperial arms, Guinian memorialized for his reinstatement and wrote the chief ministers: "Our ancestors would shift routine appointments to vindicate the remonstrance offices; they never shifted remonstrance officers to gratify a favored courtier."

sentences.zh: 兼魏王府教授，遷國子監丞。

translations.literal: He also served as lecturer to the Prince of Wei's household and was promoted to vice director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was also appointed tutor to the Prince of Wei's household and promoted to vice director of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 以侍御史林大中薦，為御史臺主簿。

translations.literal: On recommendation of Attending Censor Lin Dazhong, he was made chief clerk of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended by Attending Censor Lin Dazhong, he became chief clerk of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 改司農寺丞，進秘書郎兼嘉王府直講。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice director of the Court of Imperial Granaries and promoted to secretary and concurrent lecturer-in-ordinary to the Prince of Jia's household.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice director of the Court of Imperial Granaries and promoted to secretary with a concurrent appointment as lecturer to the Prince of Jia's household.

sentences.zh: 光宗嘗親郊，值暴風雨感疾，大臣希得進見。

translations.literal: Emperor Guangzong once personally performed the suburban sacrifice; he was stricken with illness during a violent windstorm, and the great ministers rarely gained audience.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangzong performed the suburban sacrifice in person, a violent storm brought on illness, and his senior ministers were seldom admitted to see him.

sentences.zh: 久之，疾平，猶疑畏不朝重華宮。

translations.literal: After a long while his illness abated, yet he still harbored doubts and fear and did not attend court at Chonghua Palace.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval his illness eased, yet he still shrank from visiting Chonghua Palace, where the retired emperor resided.

sentences.zh: 龜年以書譙趙汝愚，且上疏言：「壽皇之事高宗，備極子道，此陛下所親睹也。

translations.literal: Guinian wrote to admonish Zhao Ruyu and also submitted a memorial saying: "In his service to Emperor Gaozong, Emperor Shouhuang fulfilled the way of a son to the utmost—this Your Majesty witnessed with your own eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Guinian wrote to admonish Zhao Ruyu and memorialized: "In serving Emperor Gaozong, the retired emperor fulfilled every duty of filial sonhood—Your Majesty saw this yourself.

sentences.zh: 況壽皇今日止有陛下一人，聖心拳拳，不言可知。

translations.literal: Moreover, today Emperor Shouhuang has only Your Majesty as his single son; his sagely heart is earnest and devoted—this needs no words to be known.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the retired emperor now has only Your Majesty as his son; his devoted heart needs no words to make plain.

sentences.zh: 特遇過宮日分，陛下或遲其行，則壽皇不容不降免到宮之旨，蓋為陛下辭責于人，使人不得以竊議陛下，其心非不願陛下之來。

translations.literal: Only when the day came for visiting the palace, if Your Majesty delayed your going, Emperor Shouhuang could not but issue an edict excusing you from coming to the palace—this was to speak your excuse to others on your behalf, so that people might not privately criticize Your Majesty; his heart was not unwilling for Your Majesty to come.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when the day for a palace visit arrived, if Your Majesty delayed, the retired emperor would issue an edict excusing your absence—shielding you from blame so that no one could whisper against you. His heart was not unwilling to see you come.

sentences.zh: 自古人君處骨肉之間，多不與外臣謀，而與小人謀之，所以交鬥日深，疑隙日大。

translations.literal: From antiquity, when sovereigns dealt with close kin, they often did not consult outer ministers but consulted petty men; hence mutual strife grew deeper day by day and suspicion and rifts grew greater.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity, when rulers handled affairs among close kin they often took counsel not from upright ministers but from petty men—so strife deepened and suspicion widened day by day.

sentences.zh: 今日兩宮萬萬無此。

translations.literal: Today between the two palaces there is absolutely nothing of this.
translations.idiomatic: Between the two palaces today there is assuredly nothing of this kind.

sentences.zh: 然臣所憂者，外無韓琦、富弼、呂誨、司馬光之臣，而小人之中，已有任守忠者在焉，惟陛下裁察。」

translations.literal: Yet what your servant fears is that outside there are no ministers like Han Qi, Fu Bi, Lü Hui, and Sima Guang, while among petty men Ren Shouzhong is already present—may Your Majesty judge and discern."
translations.idiomatic: Yet what I fear is that outside there are no ministers of the caliber of Han Qi, Fu Bi, Lü Hui, and Sima Guang, while among petty men Ren Shouzhong is already at hand—may Your Majesty judge and discern."

sentences.zh: 又言：「使陛下虧過宮定省之禮，皆左右小人間諜之罪。

translations.literal: He also said: "If Your Majesty falls short in the rites of visiting the palace and making daily inquiries, the fault lies entirely with the petty men at your side who sow discord.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Any failure in Your Majesty's duty to visit the palace and inquire after your father is the crime of the petty men at your side who sow discord between you.

sentences.zh: 宰執侍從但能推父子之愛，調停重華；

translations.literal: The chief ministers and attendant officials can only promote the love between father and son and mediate at Chonghua;
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers and attendants can only urge the love between father and son and mediate at Chonghua Palace;

sentences.zh: 臺諫但能仗父子之義，責望人主。

translations.literal: the censorate and remonstrance officials can only rely on the righteousness between father and son and press their demands on the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: the censorate and remonstrance officials can only invoke the bond between father and son and hold the sovereign to account.

sentences.zh: 至於疑間之根，盤固不去，曾無一語及之。

translations.literal: As for the root of suspicion and estrangement, firmly entrenched and not removed, not a single word has been spoken about it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet as for the root of suspicion and estrangement, firmly entrenched and unaddressed, not one word has been said about it.

sentences.zh: 今內侍間諜兩宮者固非一人，獨陳源在壽皇朝得罪至重，近復進用，外人皆謂離間之機必自源始。

translations.literal: Today among inner attendants who sow discord between the two palaces there is certainly more than one person; Chen Yuan alone incurred the gravest guilt in Emperor Shouhuang's reign and has recently been employed again—outsiders all say the occasion for estrangement must begin with Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Today more than one inner attendant sows discord between the two palaces; Chen Yuan alone incurred the gravest guilt under the retired emperor and has lately been re-employed—outsiders all say estrangement must begin with him.

sentences.zh: 宜亟發威斷，首逐陳源，然後肅命鑾輿，負罪引慝，以謝壽皇，使父子歡然，宗社有永，顧不幸歟？」

translations.literal: Your Majesty should swiftly exercise decisive authority, first expelling Chen Yuan; then solemnly order the imperial carriage, acknowledge guilt and draw out your faults, and apologize to Emperor Shouhuang, so that father and son may be joyful together and the altars of state endure forever—would that not be fortunate?"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should swiftly act with decisive authority, expel Chen Yuan first, then order the imperial carriage in due form, acknowledge your faults, and make amends to the retired emperor, so that father and son may be reconciled and the altars of state endure—would that not be fortunate?"

sentences.zh: 居亡何，光宗朝重華，都人歡悅。

translations.literal: Before long, Emperor Guangzong attended court at Chonghua, and the people of the capital rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Emperor Guangzong visited Chonghua Palace, and the people of the capital rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 尋除起居舍人，入謝，光宗曰：「此官以待有學識人，念非卿無可者。」

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed recorder of the sovereign's daily activities; on entering to give thanks, Emperor Guangzong said: "This office awaits a man of learning and ability; considering the matter, there is no one but you."
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed recorder of the sovereign's daily activities; when he came to give thanks, Emperor Guangzong said: "This post is reserved for a man of learning; I can think of no one but you."

sentences.zh: 龜年述祖宗之法為《內治聖鑒》以進。

translations.literal: Guinian set forth the ancestral laws in a work entitled Sagely Mirror of Inner Governance and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: Guinian compiled the ancestral household regulations into Sagely Mirror of Inner Governance and presented it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 光宗曰：「祖宗家法甚善。」

translations.literal: Emperor Guangzong said: "The ancestral household regulations are very good."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangzong said: "The ancestral household regulations are excellent."

sentences.zh: 龜年曰：「臣是書大抵為宦官、女謁之防，此曹若見，恐不得數經御覽。」

translations.literal: Guinian said: "Your servant's book is largely a guard against eunuchs and female attendants; if this lot should see it, I fear it may not often pass before Your Majesty's perusal."
translations.idiomatic: Guinian said: "This book is largely a guard against eunuchs and palace women; if they see it, I fear it may not often reach Your Majesty's eyes."

sentences.zh: 光宗曰：「不至是。」

translations.literal: Emperor Guangzong said: "It will not come to that."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangzong said: "It will not come to that."

sentences.zh: 他日，龜年奏：「臣所居之官，以記注人君言動為職，車駕不過宮問安，如此書者又數十矣，恐非所以示後。」

translations.literal: On another day Guinian memorialized: "The office your servant holds has as its duty to record the sovereign's words and actions; the imperial carriage has not visited the palace to inquire after well-being, and entries of this kind number in the tens already—I fear this is not how to set an example for posterity."
translations.idiomatic: On another day Guinian memorialized: "My office records the sovereign's words and deeds; the imperial carriage has not visited the palace to inquire after your father, and there are already dozens of such entries—I fear this is no example for posterity."

sentences.zh: 有旨幸玉津園，龜年奏：「不奉三宮，而獨出宴遊，非禮也。」

translations.literal: An edict was issued to visit the Jade Ford Garden; Guinian memorialized: "Not attending the three palaces yet going out alone for feasting and pleasure is contrary to ritual."
translations.idiomatic: When an edict ordered a visit to the Jade Ford Garden, Guinian memorialized: "To feast and roam abroad without attending the three palaces is contrary to ritual."

sentences.zh: 又言：「陛下誤以臣充嘉王府講讀官，正欲臣等教以君臣父子之道。

translations.literal: He also said: "Your Majesty mistakenly appointed your servant lecturer and reader to the Prince of Jia's household—precisely because Your Majesty wished us to teach the way of ruler and minister, father and son.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Your Majesty appointed me lecturer to the Prince of Jia's household precisely so that we might teach the bonds of ruler and minister, father and son.

sentences.zh: 臣聞有身教，有言教，陛下以身教，臣以言教者也，言豈若身之切哉。」

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that there is teaching by personal example and teaching by words; Your Majesty teaches by personal example and your servant teaches by words—how can words compare in immediacy to the person?"
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that there is teaching by example and teaching by words; Your Majesty teaches by example and I by words—how can words compare in force to the example you set?"

sentences.zh: 紹熙五年五月，壽皇不豫，疾浸革，龜年連三疏請對，不獲命。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fifth year of Shaoxi, Emperor Shouhuang was unwell and his illness gradually worsened; Guinian submitted three successive memorials requesting audience but received no permission.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Shaoxi 5 (1194), the retired emperor fell ill and his condition worsened; Guinian submitted three memorials requesting audience but received no reply.

sentences.zh: 屬上視朝，龜年不離班位，伏地扣額久不已，血漬甃甓。

translations.literal: When the sovereign came to hold court, Guinian did not leave his place in the ranks; he prostrated himself and knocked his forehead on the ground for a long time without cease, and blood stained the paving bricks.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor came to court, Guinian would not leave his place in the ranks; he prostrated himself and knocked his forehead on the ground until blood stained the paving stones.

sentences.zh: 光宗曰：「素知卿忠直，欲何言？」

translations.literal: Emperor Guangzong said: "I have long known your loyalty and forthrightness—what do you wish to say?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangzong said: "I have long known your loyalty and forthrightness—what do you wish to say?"

sentences.zh: 龜年奏：「今日無大於不過宮。」

translations.literal: Guinian memorialized: "Today there is nothing greater than failure to visit the palace."
translations.idiomatic: Guinian replied: "Today there is no matter greater than Your Majesty's failure to visit the palace."

sentences.zh: 光宗曰：「須用去。」

translations.literal: Emperor Guangzong said: "I must go."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangzong said: "I must go."

sentences.zh: 龜年言：「陛下屢許臣，一入宮則又不然。

translations.literal: Guinian said: "Your Majesty has repeatedly promised your servant, yet once inside the palace it is again not so.
translations.idiomatic: Guinian said: "Your Majesty has repeatedly promised me, yet once you enter the palace it is again not so.

sentences.zh: 內外不通，臣實痛心。」

translations.literal: Inner and outer are not in communication—your servant is truly pained at heart."
translations.idiomatic: Court and palace do not communicate—I am truly heartsick."

sentences.zh: 同知樞密院余端禮曰：「扣額龍墀，曲致忠懇，臣子至此，為得已邪？」

translations.literal: Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Yu Duanli said: "Knocking his forehead on the dragon steps and bending every effort to express loyal earnestness—a subject driven to this—is it something he would do if he had any choice?"
translations.idiomatic: Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Yu Duanli said: "To knock his forehead on the dragon steps and bend every effort to express loyal earnestness—a subject driven to this point—does he do so willingly?"

sentences.zh: 上云：「知之。」

translations.literal: The sovereign said: "I understand."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "I understand."

sentences.zh: 孝宗崩，寧宗受禪，是夕召對，寧宗蹙額云：「前但聞建儲之義，豈知遽踐大位，泣辭不獲，至今震悸。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozong died, Emperor Ningzong received the abdication; that evening he was summoned for audience. Ningzong knit his brow and said: "Before I had only heard of the principle of establishing an heir—how could I know I would suddenly ascend the great throne? I wept and declined but was not permitted; to this day I am shaken and fearful."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozong died, Ningzong received the abdication; that evening Guinian was summoned. Ningzong knit his brow and said: "I had only heard of establishing an heir—how could I know I would suddenly ascend the throne? I wept and declined but was not permitted; to this day I am shaken and afraid."

sentences.zh: 龜年奏：「此乃宗祏所係，陛下安得辭，今日但當盡人子事親之誠而已。」

translations.literal: Guinian memorialized: "This concerns the altars of the ancestral temple—how can Your Majesty decline? Today you need only fulfill the sincerity of a son in serving your parent."
translations.idiomatic: Guinian replied: "This concerns the altars of state—how can Your Majesty decline? Today you need only fulfill every duty of a son toward your father."

sentences.zh: 因擬起居劄子，乞日進一通。

translations.literal: Thereupon he drafted a memorial on daily activities, requesting that one be submitted each day.
translations.idiomatic: He then drafted a memorial on daily activities, requesting that one be submitted each day.

sentences.zh: 又與翊善黃裳同奏往朝南內，因定過宮之禮，乞先一日入奏，率百官恭謝。

translations.literal: Together with Companion Huang Chang he also memorialized on proceeding to attend the Southern Inner Palace, and thereby established the rites for visiting the palace; they requested to enter and memorialize one day in advance and lead all officials in reverent thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Companion Huang Chang he memorialized on proceeding to the Southern Inner Palace, established the rites for palace visits, and requested to memorialize one day in advance and lead all officials in reverent thanks.

sentences.zh: 寧宗朝泰安宮，至則寢門已閉，拜表而退。

translations.literal: Emperor Ningzong attended Tai'an Palace; when he arrived the sleeping gate was already closed, and he presented a memorial and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Ningzong proceeded to Tai'an Palace; when he arrived the sleeping gate was already closed, so he presented a memorial and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 時議欲別建泰安宮，而光宗無徙宮之意。

translations.literal: At the time discussion favored building a separate Tai'an Palace, but Emperor Guangzong had no intention of moving palaces.
translations.idiomatic: At the time some proposed building a separate Tai'an Palace, but Guangzong had no intention of moving.

sentences.zh: 龜年言：「古人披荊棘立朝廷，尚可布政出令，況重華一宮豈為不足哉？

translations.literal: Guinian said: "The ancients, clearing brambles to establish the court, could still promulgate policies and issue orders—how much less can a single palace like Chonghua be insufficient?
translations.idiomatic: Guinian said: "The ancients cleared brambles to establish their courts and still governed effectively—how can Chonghua Palace alone be insufficient?

sentences.zh: 陛下居狹處，太上居寬處，天下之人必有諒陛下之心者。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty would dwell in a narrow place while the retired sovereign dwelt in a spacious one—among all under Heaven there would surely be those who understood Your Majesty's heart."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty would dwell in cramped quarters while the retired sovereign dwelt in spacious ones—surely the people of the realm would understand Your Majesty's heart."

sentences.zh: 於是宮不果建。

translations.literal: Thereupon the palace was not built after all.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the new palace was not built.

sentences.zh: 遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was transferred to drafter of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to drafter of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 劉慶祖已帶遙郡承宣使，而以太上隨龍人落階官，龜年繳奏，寧宗批：「可與書行。」

translations.literal: Liu Qingzu already held the rank of commissioner with the insignia of a distant commandery, yet as a follower of the retired sovereign at his accession he was reduced in rank; Guinian returned the memorial with objection. Ningzong annotated: "May be drafted and issued."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qingzu already held the rank of commissioner with the insignia of a distant commandery, yet as a follower of the retired sovereign at his accession he was demoted in rank; Guinian returned the memorial with objection. Ningzong annotated: "May be drafted and issued."

sentences.zh: 龜年奏：「臣非為慶祖惜此一官，為朝廷惜此一門耳。

translations.literal: Guinian memorialized: "Your servant is not cherishing this one office for Qingzu but cherishing this one gate of policy for the court.
translations.idiomatic: Guinian memorialized: "I am not concerned for Qingzu's single office but for a single gate of policy for the court.

sentences.zh: 夫『可與書行』，近世弊令也，使其可行，臣即書矣，使不可行，豈敢因再令而遂書哉？」

translations.literal: The phrase 'may be drafted and issued' is a corrupt order of recent times: if the matter may proceed, your servant would draft it at once; if it may not proceed, how dare your servant draft it merely because of a second order?"
translations.idiomatic: The phrase 'may be drafted and issued' is a corrupt practice of recent times: if the matter may proceed, I would draft it at once; if it may not, how dare I draft it merely because of a second order?"

sentences.zh: 寧宗嘗謂：「退朝無事，恐自怠惰，非多讀書不可。」

translations.literal: Ningzong once said: "After leaving court with nothing to do, I fear I may grow idle—one cannot do without much reading."
translations.idiomatic: Ningzong once said: "After court with nothing to do, I fear I may grow idle—one cannot do without much reading."

sentences.zh: 龜年奏：「人君之學與書生異，惟能虛心受諫，遷善改過，乃聖學中第一事，豈在多哉！」

translations.literal: Guinian memorialized: "A sovereign's learning differs from a student's; only the ability to receive remonstrance with an open mind and to move toward goodness and reform faults is the foremost matter in sagely learning—how could it lie in quantity?"
translations.idiomatic: Guinian replied: "A sovereign's learning differs from a student's; the foremost matter in sagely learning is to receive remonstrance with an open mind and to reform one's faults—how could it lie in quantity?"

sentences.zh: 一日，御筆書朱熹、黃裳、陳傅良、彭龜年、黃由、沈有開、李巘、京鏜、黃艾、鄧馹十人姓名示龜年云：「十人可充講官否？」

translations.literal: One day the emperor's own brush wrote the names of Zhu Xi, Huang Chang, Chen Fuliang, Peng Guinian, Huang You, Shen Youkai, Li Yan, Jing Tang, Huang Ai, and Deng Yi—ten men—and showed them to Guinian, saying: "Can these ten serve as lecturers?"
translations.idiomatic: One day the emperor wrote in his own hand the names of Zhu Xi, Huang Chang, Chen Fuliang, Peng Guinian, Huang You, Shen Youkai, Li Yan, Jing Tang, Huang Ai, and Deng Yi and showed them to Guinian, asking: "Can these ten serve as lecturers?"

sentences.zh: 龜年對曰：「陛下若招來一世之傑如朱熹輩，方厭人望，不可專以潛邸學官為之。」

translations.literal: Guinian replied: "If Your Majesty would summon outstanding men of the age such as Zhu Xi, you would just satisfy public expectation—you should not appoint them solely from among the study officials of the hidden residence."
translations.idiomatic: Guinian replied: "If Your Majesty would summon outstanding men of the age such as Zhu Xi, you would satisfy public expectation—you should not limit such appointments to the study officials of your princely household."

sentences.zh: 尋除侍講，遷吏部侍郎，升兼侍讀。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed lecturer-in-waiting, transferred to vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel, and promoted to concurrent reader-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed lecturer-in-waiting, transferred to vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel, and promoted to concurrent reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 龜年知事勢將變，會暴雨震雷，因極陳小人竊權、號令不時之弊。

translations.literal: Guinian knew the situation was about to change; when violent rain and thunder occurred, he therefore set forth at length the abuses of petty men usurping power and orders issued at improper times.
translations.idiomatic: Guinian sensed that affairs were about to change; when violent rain and thunder struck, he set forth at length the abuses of petty men usurping power and orders issued at improper times.

sentences.zh: 遣充金國弔祭接送伴使。

translations.literal: He was dispatched as envoy to the Jin state for condolence sacrifices and as escort and reception commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was dispatched as envoy to the Jin for condolence sacrifices and as escort and reception commissioner.

sentences.zh: 初，朱熹與龜年約共論韓侂胄之姦，會龜年護客，熹以上疏見絀，龜年聞之，附奏云：「始臣約熹同論此事。

translations.literal: Earlier Zhu Xi and Guinian had agreed to criticize Han Tuozhou's wickedness together; when Guinian was escorting envoys, Xi was demoted for submitting a memorial. When Guinian heard of it, he appended a memorial saying: "At first your servant agreed with Xi to discuss this matter together.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhu Xi and Guinian had agreed to criticize Han Tuozhou's wickedness together; when Guinian was escorting envoys, Xi was demoted for his memorial. When Guinian heard of it, he appended a memorial: "At first I agreed with Xi to discuss this matter together.

sentences.zh: 今熹既罷，臣宜並斥。」

translations.literal: Now that Xi has been dismissed, your servant should be dismissed together."
translations.idiomatic: Now that Xi has been dismissed, I should be dismissed as well."

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No response was given.
translations.idiomatic: No response was given.

sentences.zh: 迨歸，見侂胄用事，權勢重于宰相，於是條數其姦，謂：「進退大臣，更易言官，皆初政最關大體者。

translations.literal: When he returned he saw Tuozhou wielding power, his authority weightier than the chief minister's; thereupon he itemized his wickedness, saying: "The appointment and dismissal of great ministers and the replacement of remonstrance officials are matters most vital to the fundamental order at the beginning of a reign.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he saw Tuozhou wielding power with authority greater than the chief minister's; he then itemized his crimes, saying: "The appointment and dismissal of great ministers and the replacement of remonstrance officials are matters most vital to the fundamental order at the beginning of a reign.

sentences.zh: 大臣或不能知，而侂胄知之，假託聲勢，竊弄威福，不去必為後患。」

translations.literal: Great ministers might not know of these matters, yet Tuozhou knew of them; borrowing others' prestige, he secretly wielded authority and favor—if he is not removed he will surely become a future calamity."
translations.idiomatic: Great ministers might not know of these matters, yet Tuozhou knew of them; borrowing others' prestige, he secretly wielded authority and favor—if he is not removed he will surely become a future calamity."

sentences.zh: 上覽奏甚駭，曰：「侂胄朕之肺腑，信而不疑，不謂如此。」

translations.literal: The sovereign, reading the memorial, was greatly alarmed and said: "Tuozhou is my own flesh and blood; I trusted him without doubt—I did not think it would be like this."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, reading the memorial, was greatly alarmed and said: "Tuozhou is my own kin; I trusted him without doubt—I did not think it would be like this."

sentences.zh: 批下中書，予侂胄祠，已乃復入。

translations.literal: The annotation was sent down to the Secretariat, granting Tuozhou a sinecure post; soon afterward he returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: The annotation was sent to the Secretariat, granting Tuozhou a sinecure post; soon afterward he returned to court.

sentences.zh: 龜年上疏求去，詔侂胄與內祠，龜年與郡，以煥章閣待制知江陵府、湖北安撫使。

translations.literal: Guinian memorialized requesting dismissal; an edict granted Tuozhou an inner sinecure and Guinian a prefecture, appointing him Hanlin academician of the Huanzhang Hall and military commissioner of Hubei while serving as prefect of Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Guinian memorialized requesting dismissal; an edict granted Tuozhou an inner sinecure and Guinian a prefecture, appointing him Hanlin academician of the Huanzhang Hall and military commissioner of Hubei while serving as prefect of Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 龜年丐祠，慶元二年，以呂棐言落職；

translations.literal: Guinian requested a sinecure; in the second year of Qingyuan, on the word of Lü Zai he was stripped of office;
translations.idiomatic: Guinian requested a sinecure; in Qingyuan 2 (1196), on Lü Zai's accusation he was stripped of office;

sentences.zh: 已而追三官，勒停。

translations.literal: soon afterward three ranks were stripped from him and he was ordered to cease service.
translations.idiomatic: soon afterward three ranks were stripped from him and he was ordered to cease service.

sentences.zh: 嘉泰元年，復元官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiatai his original office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiatai 1 (1201) his original office was restored.

sentences.zh: 起知贛州，以疾辭，除集英殿修撰、提舉沖佑觀。

translations.literal: He was recalled to serve as prefect of Ganzhou but declined on grounds of illness and was appointed compiler at the Hall for Assembling Excellence and commissioner of the Chongyou Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as prefect of Ganzhou but declined on grounds of illness and was appointed compiler at the Hall for Assembling Excellence and commissioner of the Chongyou Abbey.

sentences.zh: 開禧二年，以待制寶謨閣致仕，卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaixi he retired with the rank of Hanlin awaiting edict of the Baomo Hall and died.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaixi 2 (1206) he retired with the rank of Hanlin awaiting edict of the Baomo Hall and died.

sentences.zh: 龜年學識正大，議論簡直，善惡是非，辨析甚嚴，其愛君憂國之忱，先見之識，敢言之氣，皆人所難。

translations.literal: Guinian's learning and knowledge were upright and great; his discourse was simple and direct; in distinguishing good and evil, right and wrong, he was very strict. His devotion in loving the ruler and worrying for the state, his foresight, and his courage to speak forth were all difficult for others.
translations.idiomatic: Guinian's learning was upright and his judgment sound; his discourse was plain and direct, and he distinguished good from evil with great rigor. His devotion to the ruler and concern for the state, his foresight, and his courage to speak forth were all beyond what most men could match.

sentences.zh: 晚既投閑，悠然自得，幾微不見於顏面。

translations.literal: In his later years, having withdrawn to leisure, he was at ease and content; the slightest trace did not show on his countenance.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years, having withdrawn to leisure, he was serene and content, and not the slightest trace of distress showed on his face.

sentences.zh: 自偽學有禁，士大夫鮮不變者，龜年于關、洛書益加涵泳，扁所居曰「止堂」，著《止堂訓蒙》，蓋始終特立者也。

translations.literal: Since the proscription on so-called heterodox learning, few among scholar-officials did not change; Guinian steeped himself all the more in the books of the Guan and Luo schools, inscribed his dwelling "Hall of Stopping," and wrote Instructions for the Young at the Hall of Stopping—thus he stood apart from first to last.
translations.idiomatic: Since the proscription on so-called heterodox learning, few scholar-officials did not bend; Guinian steeped himself all the more in the books of the Guan and Luo schools, named his dwelling Hall of Stopping, and wrote Instructions for the Young at the Hall of Stopping—thus he stood apart from first to last.

sentences.zh: 聞蘇師旦建節，曰：「此韓氏之陽虎，其禍韓氏必矣。」

translations.literal: When he heard that Su Shidan was granted a military commission, he said: "This is the Yang Hu of the Han clan—his calamity to the Han clan is certain."
translations.idiomatic: When he heard that Su Shidan was granted a military commission, he said: "This is the Yang Hu of the Han clan—his calamity to the Han clan is certain."

sentences.zh: 及聞用兵，曰：「禍其在此乎？」

translations.literal: When he heard that war was launched, he said: "Is the calamity here?"
translations.idiomatic: When he heard that war was launched, he said: "Is the calamity here?"

sentences.zh: 所著書有《經解》、《祭儀》、《五致錄》、奏議、外制。

translations.literal: His written works include Exegesis of the Classics, Sacrificial Rites, Record of the Five Tributes, memorials, and outer drafts.
translations.idiomatic: His written works include Exegesis of the Classics, Sacrificial Rites, Record of the Five Tributes, memorials, and outer drafts.

sentences.zh: 侂胄誅，林大中、樓錀皆白其忠，寧宗詔贈寶謨閣直學士。

translations.literal: After Tuozhou was executed, Lin Dazhong and Lou Yue both reported his loyalty, and Emperor Ningzong issued an edict posthumously granting him academician of the Baomo Hall.
translations.idiomatic: After Tuozhou was executed, Lin Dazhong and Lou Yue both reported his loyalty, and Ningzong issued an edict posthumously granting him academician of the Baomo Hall.

sentences.zh: 章穎等請易名，賜諡「忠肅」。

translations.literal: Zhang Ying and others requested a change of posthumous name, and the posthumous title Loyal and Solemn was bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ying and others requested a posthumous name, and the posthumous title Loyal and Solemn was bestowed.

sentences.zh: 上謂穎等曰：「彭龜年忠鯁可嘉，宜得諡。

translations.literal: The sovereign said to Ying and the others: "Peng Guinian's loyal forthrightness is worthy of praise; he should receive a posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Ying and the others: "Peng Guinian's loyal forthrightness is worthy of praise; he should receive a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 使人人如此，必能納君於無過之地。」

translations.literal: If every man were like this, the ruler could surely be brought to a place without fault."
translations.idiomatic: If every man were like this, the ruler could surely be kept without fault."

sentences.zh: 未幾，加贈龍圖閣學士，而擢用其子欽。

translations.literal: Before long he was further granted academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall, and his son Qin was promoted and employed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was further granted academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall, and his son Qin was promoted and employed.

sentences.zh: 黃裳，字文叔，隆慶府普成人。

translations.literal: Huang Chang, courtesy name Wenshu, was a native of Pucheng in Longqing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chang, styled Wenshu, came from Pucheng in Longqing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少穎異，能屬文。

translations.literal: In youth he was exceptionally keen and could compose literary works.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was exceptionally gifted and could compose literary works.

sentences.zh: 登乾道五年進士第，調巴州通江尉。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Qiandao he passed the jinshi examination and was assigned as registrar of Tongjiang in Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: He placed on the jinshi roll in Qiandao 5 (1169) and was posted as registrar of Tongjiang in Ba Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 益務進學，文詞迥出流輩，人見之曰：「非復前日文叔矣。」

translations.literal: He strove all the more to advance his learning; his literary compositions far surpassed his contemporaries, and when people saw him they said: "He is no longer the Wenshu of former days."
translations.idiomatic: He strove all the more to advance his learning; his literary compositions far surpassed his contemporaries, and when people saw him they said: "He is no longer the Wenshu of former days."

sentences.zh: 時蜀中餉師，名為和糴，實則取民。

translations.literal: At the time in Shu they supplied the army; it was called harmonized purchase but in fact took from the people.
translations.idiomatic: At the time in Shu they supplied the army under the name of harmonized purchase, but in fact they took from the people.

sentences.zh: 裳賦《漢中行》，諷總領李蘩，蘩為罷糴，民便之。

translations.literal: Chang composed "Journey in Hanzhong," satirizing the overall commander Li Fan; Fan thereupon abolished the purchase system, and the people were benefited.
translations.idiomatic: Chang composed "Journey in Hanzhong," satirizing the overall commander Li Fan; Fan abolished the purchase system, and the people were relieved.

sentences.zh: 改興元府錄事參軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to recorder of Xingyuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to recorder of Xingyuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以四川制置使留正薦，召對，論蜀兵民大計。

translations.literal: On recommendation of Liu Zheng, commissioner of Sichuan, he was summoned for audience and discussed the great plan for troops and people in Shu.
translations.idiomatic: On recommendation of Liu Zheng, commissioner of Sichuan, he was summoned for audience and discussed the great plan for troops and people in Shu.

sentences.zh: 遷國子博士，以母喪去。

translations.literal: He was transferred to doctorate of the Imperial University and left office on his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to doctorate of the Imperial University and left office on his mother's death.

sentences.zh: 宰相進擬他官，上問裳安在，賜錢七十萬。

translations.literal: The chief minister advanced nominations for other offices; the sovereign asked where Chang was and bestowed seventy thousand in cash.
translations.idiomatic: When the chief minister advanced nominations for other offices, the emperor asked where Chang was and bestowed seventy thousand in cash.

sentences.zh: 除喪，復召。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was summoned again.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was summoned again.

sentences.zh: 時光宗登極，裳進對，謂：「中興規模與守成不同，出攻入守，當據利便之勢，不可不定行都。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Guangzong had ascended the throne; Chang presented himself for audience and said: "The scale of the Restoration differs from that of preserving an established reign; in advancing to attack and withdrawing to defend, one should hold to advantageous positions—a mobile capital cannot be left undecided.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangzong had ascended the throne, Chang presented himself for audience and said: "The scale of the Restoration differs from that of preserving an established reign; in advancing to attack and withdrawing to defend, one must hold advantageous positions—a mobile capital cannot be left undecided.

sentences.zh: 富國強兵，當求功利之實，不可不課吏治。

translations.literal: To enrich the state and strengthen the army, one should seek the substance of utility and merit and cannot fail to examine official governance.
translations.idiomatic: To enrich the state and strengthen the army, one must seek real results in utility and merit and cannot neglect to examine official governance.

sentences.zh: 捍內禦外，當有緩急之備，不可不立重鎮。」

translations.literal: To defend within and resist without, one should have preparations for urgency and ease and cannot fail to establish strategic strongholds."
translations.idiomatic: To defend within and resist without, one must prepare for both urgency and ease and cannot fail to establish strategic strongholds."

sentences.zh: 其論行都，以為就便利之勢，莫若建康。

translations.literal: In his discussion of the mobile capital, he held that with regard to advantageous position, none was better than Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: On the mobile capital, he held that for advantageous position none was better than Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 其論吏治，謂立品式以課其功，計資考以久其任。

translations.literal: In his discussion of official governance, he said that standards and forms should be established to assess merit and seniority and examination should be calculated to prolong tenure in office.
translations.idiomatic: On official governance, he said that standards should be established to assess merit and that seniority and examination should be used to prolong tenure in office.

sentences.zh: 其論重鎮，謂自吳至蜀，綿亙萬里，曰漢中，曰襄陽，曰江陵，曰鄂渚，曰京口，當為五鎮，以將相大臣守之，五鎮強則國體重矣。

translations.literal: In his discussion of strategic strongholds, he said that from Wu to Shu, stretching ten thousand li, there were Hanzhong, Xiangyang, Jiangling, Ezhou, and Jingkou—they should be made five garrisons, guarded by generals, ministers, and great officials; when the five garrisons were strong, the body of the state would be weighty.
translations.idiomatic: On strategic strongholds, he said that from Wu to Shu, stretching ten thousand li, Hanzhong, Xiangyang, Jiangling, Ezhou, and Jingkou should be made five garrisons, guarded by generals and great ministers; when the five garrisons were strong, the state would be secure.

sentences.zh: 除太學博士，進秘書郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed erudite of the Imperial University and promoted to secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed erudite of the Imperial University and promoted to secretary.

sentences.zh: 遷嘉王府翊善，講《春秋》「王正月」 曰：「周之王，即今之帝也。

translations.literal: He was transferred to companion of the Prince of Jia's household; lecturing on the Spring and Autumn Annals passage "the King's first month," he said: "The king of Zhou is today's emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to companion of the Prince of Jia's household; lecturing on the Spring and Autumn Annals passage "the King's first month," he said: "The king of Zhou is today's emperor.

sentences.zh: 王不能號令諸侯，則王不足為王；

translations.literal: If a king cannot command the feudal lords, then he is not sufficient to be a king;
translations.idiomatic: If a king cannot command the feudal lords, he is not truly a king;

sentences.zh: 帝不能統御郡鎮，則帝不足為帝。

translations.literal: if an emperor cannot govern and control prefectures and garrisons, then he is not sufficient to be an emperor.
translations.idiomatic: if an emperor cannot govern prefectures and garrisons, he is not truly an emperor.

sentences.zh: 今之郡縣，即古諸侯也。

translations.literal: Today's prefectures and counties are the feudal lords of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Today's prefectures and counties are the feudal lords of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 周之王惟不能號令諸侯，故《春秋》必書 『王正月』，所以一諸侯之正朔。

translations.literal: The king of Zhou precisely because he could not command the feudal lords, therefore the Spring and Autumn Annals must record "the King's first month"—thereby to unify the calendar of the feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: Because the king of Zhou could not command the feudal lords, the Spring and Autumn Annals must record "the King's first month"—thereby to unify the calendar of the feudal lords.

sentences.zh: 今天下境土，比祖宗時不能十之四，然猶跨吳、蜀、荊、廣、閩、越二百州，任吾民者，二百州守也，任吾兵者，九都統也，苟不能統御，則何以服之？」

translations.literal: Today the realm's territory, compared with the time of the ancestral emperors, is not even four-tenths; yet it still spans Wu, Shu, Jing, Guang, Min, and Yue—two hundred prefectures. Those who bear charge for our people are the two hundred prefects; those who bear charge for our troops are the nine commanders-in-chief—if one cannot govern and control them, how can one make them submit?"
translations.idiomatic: Today our territory is not even four-tenths of what it was under the ancestral emperors; yet it still spans Wu, Shu, Jing, Guang, Min, and Yue—two hundred prefectures. The two hundred prefects bear charge for our people; the nine commanders-in-chief bear charge for our troops—if you cannot govern them, how can you make them submit?"

sentences.zh: 王曰：「何謂九都統？」

translations.literal: The prince said: "What are the nine commanders-in-chief?"
translations.idiomatic: The prince said: "What are the nine commanders-in-chief?"

sentences.zh: 裳曰：「唐太宗年十八起義兵，平禍亂。

translations.literal: Chang said: "Emperor Taizong of Tang at age eighteen raised righteous troops and pacified calamity and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Chang said: "Emperor Taizong of Tang at age eighteen raised righteous troops and pacified calamity and disorder.

sentences.zh: 今大王年過之，而國家九都統之說猶有未知，其可不汲汲於學乎？」

translations.literal: Today the great prince has passed that age, yet the state's doctrine of the nine commanders-in-chief is still unknown to you—how can you not urgently devote yourself to learning?"
translations.idiomatic: Today you have passed that age, yet you still do not know the state's doctrine of the nine commanders-in-chief—how can you not urgently devote yourself to learning?"

sentences.zh: 他日，王擢用東宮舊人吳端，端詣王謝，王接之中節。

translations.literal: On another day the prince promoted Wu Duan, an old associate of the Eastern Palace; Duan came to thank the prince, and the prince received him with proper measure.
translations.idiomatic: On another day the prince promoted Wu Duan, an old associate of the Eastern Palace; Duan came to thank the prince, and the prince received him with proper measure.

sentences.zh: 裳因講《左氏》「禮有等衰」，問王：「比待吳端得重輕之節，有之乎？」

translations.literal: Chang thereupon lectured on the Zuo Commentary passage "rites have gradations of decrease," and asked the prince: "In receiving Wu Duan recently, did you observe the measure of greater and lesser?"
translations.idiomatic: Chang thereupon lectured on the Zuo Commentary passage "rites have gradations of decrease," and asked the prince: "In receiving Wu Duan recently, did you observe the measure of greater and lesser?"

sentences.zh: 王曰：「有之。」

translations.literal: The prince said: "I did."
translations.idiomatic: The prince said: "I did."

sentences.zh: 裳曰：「王者之學，正當見諸行事。

translations.literal: Chang said: "A king's learning should precisely be manifested in conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Chang said: "A king's learning should be manifested in conduct.

sentences.zh: 今王臨事有區別，是得等衰之義矣。」

translations.literal: Today in affairs the prince makes distinctions—this is obtaining the meaning of gradations of decrease."
translations.idiomatic: Today in affairs you make distinctions—this is obtaining the meaning of gradations of decrease."

sentences.zh: 王意益向學。

translations.literal: The prince's mind turned all the more toward learning.
translations.idiomatic: The prince's mind turned all the more toward learning.

sentences.zh: 於是作八圖以獻：曰太極，曰三才本性，曰皇帝王伯學術，曰九流學術，曰天文，曰地理，曰帝王紹運，以百官終焉，各述大旨陳之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he composed eight diagrams to present: entitled Supreme Polarity, Nature of the Three Powers, Learning of Emperors, Kings, Hegemons, and Lords, Learning of the Nine Schools, Astronomy, Geography, and Succession of Emperors and Kings, ending with the hundred officials—each he set forth its main purport.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he composed eight diagrams to present: Supreme Polarity, Nature of the Three Powers, Learning of Emperors, Kings, Hegemons, and Lords, Learning of the Nine Schools, Astronomy, Geography, Succession of Emperors and Kings, and the hundred officials—each he set forth its main purport.

sentences.zh: 每進言曰：「為學之道，當體之以心。

translations.literal: Whenever he offered counsel he said: "The way of learning should be embodied in the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he offered counsel he said: "The way of learning must be embodied in the heart.

sentences.zh: 王宜以心為嚴師，於心有一毫不安者，不可為也。」

translations.literal: The prince should take the heart as his strict teacher; where in the heart there is the slightest unease, one must not act."
translations.idiomatic: You should take your heart as your strict teacher; where your heart feels the slightest unease, you must not act."

sentences.zh: 且引前代危亡之事以為儆戒。

translations.literal: Moreover he cited instances of peril and ruin in former ages as warnings.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover he cited instances of peril and ruin in former ages as warnings.

sentences.zh: 王謂人曰：「黃翊善之言，人所難堪，惟我能受之。」

translations.literal: The prince said to others: "Companion Huang's words are what others find hard to bear—only I can receive them."
translations.idiomatic: The prince said to others: "Companion Huang's words are what others find hard to bear—only I can receive them."

sentences.zh: 他日，王過重華宮，壽皇問所讀書，王舉以對，壽皇曰：「數不太多乎？」

translations.literal: On another day the prince passed Chonghua Palace; Emperor Shouhuang asked what books he was reading, and the prince listed them in reply. Emperor Shouhuang said: "Are they not rather too many?"
translations.idiomatic: On another day the prince passed Chonghua Palace; the retired emperor asked what books he was reading, and the prince listed them in reply. The retired emperor said: "Are they not rather too many?"

sentences.zh: 王曰：「講官訓說明白，忱心樂之，不知其多也。」

translations.literal: The prince said: "The lecturer explains clearly; I delight in it with earnest heart and do not notice how many there are."
translations.idiomatic: The prince said: "The lecturer explains clearly; I delight in it with earnest heart and do not notice how many there are."

sentences.zh: 壽皇曰：「黃翊善至誠，所講須諦聽之。」

translations.literal: Emperor Shouhuang said: "Companion Huang is utterly sincere—what he lectures you must listen to attentively."
translations.idiomatic: The retired emperor said: "Companion Huang is utterly sincere—what he lectures you must listen to attentively."

sentences.zh: 裳久侍王邸，每歲誕節，則陳詩以寓諷。

translations.literal: Chang long served at the prince's residence; each year on his birthday he would present poems to convey admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Chang long served at the prince's residence; each year on his birthday he would present poems to convey admonition.

sentences.zh: 初嘗制渾天儀、輿地圖，侑以詩章，欲王觀象則知進學，如天運之不息，披圖則思祖宗境土半陷於異域而未歸。

translations.literal: At first he made a armillary sphere and a terrestrial map, accompanying them with poems, wishing that when the prince observed the heavens he would know to advance in learning, as the celestial motion never ceases, and when he unrolled the map he would think how the ancestral emperors' territory was half lost to foreign lands and not yet recovered.
translations.idiomatic: At first he made an armillary sphere and a terrestrial map, accompanying them with poems, wishing that when the prince observed the heavens he would know to advance in learning, as the celestial motion never ceases, and when he unrolled the map he would think how half the ancestral territory was lost to foreign lands and not yet recovered.

sentences.zh: 其後又以王所講三經為詩三章以進。

translations.literal: Later he also composed three poems on the three classics the prince had studied and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: Later he also composed three poems on the three classics the prince had studied and presented them.

sentences.zh: 王喜，為置酒，手書其詩以賜之。

translations.literal: The prince was pleased, set out wine, and in his own hand wrote out the poems to bestow on him.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was pleased, set out wine, and in his own hand wrote out the poems to bestow on him.

sentences.zh: 王嘗侍宴宮中，從容為光宗誦《酒誥》，曰：「此黃翊善所教也。」

translations.literal: The prince once attended a banquet in the palace and at leisure recited the "Admonition on Wine" for Emperor Guangzong, saying: "This is what Companion Huang taught."
translations.idiomatic: The prince once attended a banquet in the palace and at leisure recited the "Admonition on Wine" for Emperor Guangzong, saying: "This is what Companion Huang taught."

sentences.zh: 光宗詔勞裳，裳曰：「臣不及朱熹，熹學問四十年，若召置府寮，宜有裨益。」

translations.literal: Emperor Guangzong issued an edict to console Chang; Chang said: "Your servant does not equal Zhu Xi; Xi has pursued learning for forty years—if summoned and placed among the prince's staff, he should be of benefit."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangzong issued an edict to console Chang; Chang said: "I do not equal Zhu Xi; Xi has pursued learning for forty years—if summoned and placed among the prince's staff, he should be of benefit."

sentences.zh: 光宗嘉納。

translations.literal: Emperor Guangzong praised and accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangzong praised and accepted this.

sentences.zh: 裳每勸講，必援古證今，即事明理，凡可以開導王心者，無不言也。

translations.literal: Whenever Chang lectured, he invariably cited antiquity to prove the present and clarified principle through immediate affairs; whatever could open and guide the prince's mind, there was nothing he did not speak of.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Chang lectured, he invariably cited antiquity to prove the present and clarified principle through immediate affairs; whatever could open and guide the prince's mind, there was nothing he did not speak of.

sentences.zh: 紹熙二年，遷起居舍人。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaoxi he was transferred to recorder of the sovereign's daily activities.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxi 2 (1191) he was transferred to recorder of the sovereign's daily activities.

sentences.zh: 奏曰：「自古人君不能從諫者，其蔽有三：一曰私心，二曰勝心，三曰忿心。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "From antiquity, when sovereigns could not accept remonstrance, their obstructions were three: first, selfish mind; second, mind of victory; third, mind of anger.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "From antiquity, when sovereigns could not accept remonstrance, their obstructions were three: selfish mind, mind of victory, and mind of anger.

sentences.zh: 事苟不出於公，而以己見執之，謂之私心；

translations.literal: If affairs do not proceed from the public good but one clings to one's own view, this is called selfish mind;
translations.idiomatic: If affairs do not proceed from the public good but one clings to one's own view, this is selfish mind;

sentences.zh: 私心生，則以諫者為病，而求以勝之；

translations.literal: when selfish mind arises, one regards remonstrators as a affliction and seeks to overcome them;
translations.idiomatic: when selfish mind arises, one regards remonstrators as an affliction and seeks to overcome them;

sentences.zh: 勝心生，則以諫者為仇，而求以逐之。

translations.literal: when mind of victory arises, one regards remonstrators as enemies and seeks to drive them away.
translations.idiomatic: when mind of victory arises, one regards remonstrators as enemies and seeks to drive them away.

sentences.zh: 因私而生勝，因勝而生忿，忿心生，則事有不得其理者焉。

translations.literal: From selfishness victory arises; from victory anger arises; when mind of anger arises, affairs have those that do not obtain their proper principle.
translations.idiomatic: From selfishness victory arises; from victory anger arises; when anger arises, affairs no longer follow their proper course.

sentences.zh: 如潘景珪，常才也，陛下固亦以常人遇之，特以臺諫攻之不已，致陛下庇之愈力，事勢相激，乃至於此。

translations.literal: Take Pan Jinggui—an ordinary talent; Your Majesty indeed also treated him as an ordinary man, but solely because the censorate and remonstrance officials attacked him without cease, it led Your Majesty to shield him all the more forcefully; affairs and circumstances mutually provoked one another until it came to this.
translations.idiomatic: Take Pan Jinggui—an ordinary talent whom Your Majesty treated as an ordinary man; solely because the censorate and remonstrance officials attacked him without cease, Your Majesty shielded him all the more forcefully—affairs and circumstances mutually provoked one another until it came to this.

sentences.zh: 宜因事靜察，使心無所係，則聞臺諫之言無不悅，而無欲勝之心，待臺諫之心無不誠，而無加忿之意矣。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty should quietly examine affairs as they arise and let the mind be bound to nothing; then in hearing the words of the censorate and remonstrance officials there would be nothing but pleasure, and no mind wishing victory; in treating the censorate and remonstrance officials there would be nothing but sincerity, and no intention of adding anger."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should quietly examine affairs as they arise and let your mind be bound to nothing; then you would hear the censorate and remonstrance officials with pleasure and without mind of victory, and treat them with sincerity and without anger."

sentences.zh: 三年，試中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the third year he was tested and appointed drafter of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was tested and appointed drafter of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時武備寢弛，裳上疏曰：「壽皇在位三十年，拊循將士，士常恨不得效死以報。

translations.literal: At the time military preparations were gradually relaxed; Chang submitted a memorial saying: "Emperor Shouhuang during thirty years on the throne comforted and guided officers and soldiers; the soldiers often regretted that they could not offer their lives in death to repay him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time military preparations were gradually relaxed; Chang submitted a memorial saying: "The retired emperor during thirty years on the throne comforted and guided officers and soldiers; they often regretted that they could not offer their lives to repay him.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠能留意武事，三軍之士孰不感激願為陛下用乎？」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty truly can attend to military affairs, which of the three armies' soldiers would not be moved with gratitude and wish to be employed by Your Majesty?"
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty truly attends to military affairs, which soldier of the three armies would not be moved with gratitude and wish to serve you?"

sentences.zh: 又論：「荊、襄形勢居吳、蜀之中，其地四平，若金人搗襄陽，據江陵，按兵以守，則吳、蜀中斷，此今日邊備之最可憂也。

translations.literal: He also discussed: "The strategic position of Jing and Xiang lies between Wu and Shu; the terrain is level on four sides. If the Jurchen strike at Xiangyang, seize Jiangling, and hold their troops to defend, then Wu and Shu would be cut off in the middle—this is what is most to be feared in today's frontier defense.
translations.idiomatic: He also discussed: "The strategic position of Jing and Xiang lies between Wu and Shu; the terrain is level on four sides. If the Jurchen strike at Xiangyang, seize Jiangling, and hold their troops to defend, Wu and Shu would be cut off in the middle—this is what is most to be feared in today's frontier defense.

sentences.zh: 宜分鄂渚兵一二萬人屯襄、漢之間，以張形勢而壯重地。」

translations.literal: Ten or twenty thousand troops from Ezhou should be divided and stationed between Xiang and Han to display strategic posture and strengthen the vital region."
translations.idiomatic: Ten or twenty thousand troops from Ezhou should be divided and stationed between Xiang and Han to display strategic posture and strengthen the vital region."

sentences.zh: 時朝廷方宴安，裳所言多不省。

translations.literal: At the time the court was just feasting in ease; what Chang spoke was mostly not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the court was feasting in ease; what Chang spoke was mostly not heeded.

sentences.zh: 未幾，除給事中。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 趙汝愚除同知樞密院，監察御史汪義端言祖宗之法，宗室不為執政，再疏醜詆汝愚，汝愚乞免官。

translations.literal: Zhao Ruyu was appointed vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs; Investigating Censor Wang Yiduan cited the ancestral law that imperial clansmen do not serve as chief ministers, and in two successive memorials vilified Ruyu; Ruyu requested dismissal from office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ruyu was appointed vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs; Investigating Censor Wang Yiduan cited the ancestral law that imperial clansmen do not serve as chief ministers and in two successive memorials vilified Ruyu; Ruyu requested dismissal from office.

sentences.zh: 裳奏：「汝愚事父孝，事君忠，居官廉。

translations.literal: Chang memorialized: "Ruyu serves his father with filial piety, serves his ruler with loyalty, and in office is incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: Chang memorialized: "Ruyu serves his father with filial piety, serves his ruler with loyalty, and in office is incorrupt.

sentences.zh: 憂國愛民，出於天性，如青天白日，奴隸知其清明。

translations.literal: His concern for the state and love for the people proceed from his inborn nature, like blue sky and white sun—even slaves know his clarity.
translations.idiomatic: His concern for the state and love for the people proceed from his inborn nature, like blue sky and white sun—even slaves know his integrity.

sentences.zh: 義端所見，皆奴隸之不如，不可以居朝列。」

translations.literal: What Yiduan sees is all beneath what slaves know—he cannot remain in the court ranks."
translations.idiomatic: What Yiduan sees is all beneath what slaves know—he cannot remain in the court ranks."

sentences.zh: 於是義端與郡。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yiduan was given a prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Yiduan was given a prefecture.

sentences.zh: 裳在瑣闥甫一月，封駁無慮十數。

translations.literal: Chang had been in the secretariat barely a month when he sealed and rejected orders numbering no fewer than ten or more.
translations.idiomatic: Chang had been in the secretariat barely a month when he sealed and rejected no fewer than ten orders.

sentences.zh: 韓侂胄落階官，鄭汝諧除吏部侍郎，裳皆繳其命。

translations.literal: Han Tuozhou was reduced in rank; Zheng Ruxie was appointed vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel—Chang returned both orders with objection.
translations.idiomatic: Han Tuozhou was reduced in rank; Zheng Ruxie was appointed vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel—Chang returned both orders with objection.

sentences.zh: 改兵部侍郎，不拜，遂以顯謨閣待制充翊善。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice minister of the Ministry of War but did not accept; thereupon he was made Hanlin awaiting edict of the Xianmo Hall and served as companion.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice minister of the Ministry of War but did not accept; thereupon he was made Hanlin awaiting edict of the Xianmo Hall and served as companion.

sentences.zh: 先是，光宗以憂疑成疾，不過重華宮，裳入疏請五日一朝，至是復苦言之。

translations.literal: Earlier Emperor Guangzong, through worry and suspicion, had fallen ill and did not visit Chonghua Palace; Chang had submitted a memorial requesting audience every five days; now he again spoke bitterly on the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Guangzong, through worry and suspicion, had fallen ill and did not visit Chonghua Palace; Chang had submitted a memorial requesting audience every five days; now he again spoke bitterly on the matter.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「內侍楊舜卿告朕勿過宮。」

translations.literal: The sovereign said: "Inner attendant Yang Shunqing told me not to visit the palace."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Inner attendant Yang Shunqing told me not to visit the palace."

sentences.zh: 裳請斬舜卿，且以八事之目為奏，曰念恩，釋怨，辨讒，去疑，責己，畏天，防亂，改過。

translations.literal: Chang requested that Shunqing be executed, and moreover memorialized under eight headings: recall kindness, release resentment, distinguish slander, remove suspicion, blame oneself, fear Heaven, guard against disorder, and reform faults.
translations.idiomatic: Chang requested that Shunqing be executed and memorialized under eight headings: recall kindness, release resentment, distinguish slander, remove suspicion, blame oneself, fear Heaven, guard against disorder, and reform faults.

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No response was given.
translations.idiomatic: No response was given.

sentences.zh: 裳嘗病疽，及是憂憤，創復作，又奏：

translations.literal: Chang had once suffered from a carbuncle; now through worry and indignation the wound broke out again, and he again memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: Chang had once suffered from a carbuncle; now through worry and indignation the wound broke out again, and he again memorialized:

sentences.zh: 「陛下之于壽皇，未盡孝敬之道，意者必有所疑也。

translations.literal: "In Your Majesty's relation to Emperor Shouhuang, you have not fully fulfilled the way of filial respect and reverence—presumably there must be some suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: "In your relation to the retired emperor, you have not fully fulfilled filial respect and reverence—presumably you harbor some suspicion.

sentences.zh: 臣竊推致疑之因，陛下毋乃以焚廩、浚井之事為憂乎？

translations.literal: Your servant ventures to infer the cause of suspicion: might Your Majesty be worried about the matters of burning the granary and digging the well?
translations.idiomatic: I venture to infer the cause of your suspicion: might you be worried about the matters of burning the granary and digging the well?

sentences.zh: 夫焚廩、浚井，在當時或有之。

translations.literal: As for burning the granary and digging the well, at the time there may have been such things.
translations.idiomatic: As for burning the granary and digging the well, at the time there may have been such things.

sentences.zh: 壽皇之子惟陛下一人，壽皇之心，託陛下甚重，愛陛下甚至，故憂陛下甚切。

translations.literal: Emperor Shouhuang's son is only Your Majesty alone; Emperor Shouhuang's heart entrusts Your Majesty with great weight, loves Your Majesty to the utmost, and therefore worries for Your Majesty most keenly.
translations.idiomatic: The retired emperor's son is only you; his heart entrusts you with great weight, loves you to the utmost, and therefore worries for you most keenly.

sentences.zh: 違豫之際，焫香祝天，為陛下祈禱。

translations.literal: When you were unwell, he burned incense and prayed to Heaven, offering prayers on Your Majesty's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: When you were unwell, he burned incense and prayed to Heaven on your behalf.

sentences.zh: 愛子如此，則焚廩、浚井之心，臣有以知其必無也，陛下何疑焉？

translations.literal: Loving his son thus, as for a heart to burn the granary and dig the well, your servant has grounds to know it surely does not exist—why should Your Majesty suspect?
translations.idiomatic: Loving his son thus, I have grounds to know he surely harbored no heart to burn the granary or dig the well—why should you suspect?

sentences.zh: 又無乃以肅宗之事為憂乎？

translations.literal: Or might you be worried about the affair of Emperor Suzong?
translations.idiomatic: Or might you be worried about the affair of Emperor Suzong?

sentences.zh: 肅宗即位靈武，非明皇意，故不能無疑。

translations.literal: Suzong ascended the throne at Lingwu—not according to Emperor Ming's intent—so suspicion could not be absent.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong ascended the throne at Lingwu—not according to Emperor Xuanzong's intent—so suspicion could not be absent.

sentences.zh: 壽皇當未倦勤，親挈神器授之陛下，揖遜之風，同符堯、舜，與明皇之事不可同日而語明矣，陛下何疑焉？

translations.literal: Emperor Shouhuang, when not yet weary of toil, personally took the sacred vessel and entrusted it to Your Majesty; the manner of yielding and retiring matches Yao and Shun—it cannot be spoken of in the same breath as Emperor Ming's affair—why should Your Majesty suspect?
translations.idiomatic: The retired emperor, when not yet weary of toil, personally took the sacred vessel and entrusted it to you; the manner of yielding and retiring matches Yao and Shun—it cannot be spoken of in the same breath as Xuanzong's affair—why should you suspect?

sentences.zh: 又無乃以衛輒之事為憂乎？

translations.literal: Or might you be worried about the affair of Wei Zhe?
translations.idiomatic: Or might you be worried about the affair of Wei Zhe?

sentences.zh: 輒與蒯聵，父子爭國。

translations.literal: Zhe and Kuai Kui, father and son, contended for the state.
translations.idiomatic: Zhe and Kuai Kui, father and son, contended for the state.

sentences.zh: 壽皇老且病，乃頤神北宮，以保康寧，而以天下事付之陛下，非有爭心也，陛下何疑焉？

translations.literal: Emperor Shouhuang is old and ill; he nurtures his spirit in the Northern Palace to preserve health and tranquility and entrusts affairs of all under Heaven to Your Majesty—there is no heart of contention; why should Your Majesty suspect?
translations.idiomatic: The retired emperor is old and ill; he nurtures his spirit in the Northern Palace to preserve health and tranquility and entrusts affairs of all under Heaven to you—there is no heart of contention; why should you suspect?

sentences.zh: 又無乃以孟子責善為疑乎？

translations.literal: Or might you suspect on account of Mencius's doctrine of holding one to goodness?
translations.idiomatic: Or might you suspect on account of Mencius's doctrine of holding one to goodness?

sentences.zh: 父子責善，本生於愛，為子者能知此理，則何至於相夷。

translations.literal: Father and son holding each other to goodness arises from love in the first place; if as son one can know this principle, how could it come to mutual destruction?
translations.idiomatic: Father and son holding each other to goodness arises from love in the first place; if as son one can know this principle, how could it come to mutual destruction?

sentences.zh: 壽皇願陛下為聖帝，責善之心出於忠愛，非賊恩也，陛下何疑焉？

translations.literal: Emperor Shouhuang wishes Your Majesty to be a sagely emperor; the heart of holding to goodness proceeds from loyal love—it is not injuring kindness; why should Your Majesty suspect?
translations.idiomatic: The retired emperor wishes you to be a sagely emperor; the heart of holding to goodness proceeds from loyal love—it is not injuring kindness; why should you suspect?

sentences.zh: 此四者，或者之所以為疑，臣以理推之，初無一之可疑者。

translations.literal: These four are perhaps the grounds for suspicion; your servant, reasoning by principle, finds not one that is grounds for suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: These four are perhaps the grounds for your suspicion; reasoning by principle, I find not one that is grounds for suspicion.

sentences.zh: 自父子之間，小有猜疑，此心一萌，方寸遂亂。

translations.literal: From the moment a little suspicion arises between father and son, once this heart sprouts, the inner mind is immediately thrown into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: From the moment a little suspicion arises between father and son, once this heart sprouts, the inner mind is immediately thrown into disorder.

sentences.zh: 故天變則疑而不知畏，民困則疑而不知恤，疑宰執專權則不禮大臣，疑臺諫生事則不受忠諫，疑嗜欲無害則近酒色，疑君子有黨則庇小人。

translations.literal: Thus when heaven sends prodigies one suspects and does not know to fear; when the people suffer hardship one suspects and does not know to pity; suspecting that chief ministers monopolize power one does not treat great ministers with ritual; suspecting that the censorate and remonstrance officials stir up affairs one does not accept loyal remonstrance; suspecting that indulgence in desires is harmless one draws near wine and women; suspecting that gentlemen form factions one shelters petty men.
translations.idiomatic: Thus when heaven sends prodigies you suspect and do not know to fear; when the people suffer you suspect and do not know to pity; suspecting that chief ministers monopolize power you do not treat great ministers with ritual; suspecting that remonstrance officials stir up affairs you do not accept loyal remonstrance; suspecting that indulgence is harmless you draw near wine and women; suspecting that gentlemen form factions you shelter petty men.

sentences.zh: 事有不須疑者，莫不以為疑。

translations.literal: Matters that need not be suspected—all are taken as suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Matters that need not be suspected—you take them all as suspicious.

sentences.zh: 乃若貴為天子，不以孝聞，敵國聞之，將肆輕侮，此可疑也，而陛下則不疑；

translations.literal: Yet if one is exalted as Son of Heaven yet is not known for filial piety, when enemy states hear of it they will indulge in contempt—this is to be suspected, yet Your Majesty does not suspect;
translations.idiomatic: Yet if you are exalted as Son of Heaven yet are not known for filial piety, when enemy states hear of it they will indulge in contempt—this is to be suspected, yet you do not suspect;

sentences.zh: 小人將起為亂，此可疑也，而陛下則不疑；

translations.literal: petty men are about to rise in disorder—this is to be suspected, yet Your Majesty does not suspect;
translations.idiomatic: petty men are about to rise in disorder—this is to be suspected, yet you do not suspect;

sentences.zh: 中外官軍，豈無他志，此可疑也，而陛下則不疑。

translations.literal: among officials and troops within and without, are there none with other intentions—this is to be suspected, yet Your Majesty does not suspect.
translations.idiomatic: among officials and troops within and without, are there none with other intentions—this is to be suspected, yet you do not suspect.

sentences.zh: 事之可疑者，反不以為疑，顛倒錯亂，莫甚於此，禍亂之萌，近在旦夕。

translations.literal: What is to be suspected is not taken as suspicious—upside down and confused, nothing exceeds this; the sprouting of calamity and disorder is close at hand, within the morrow.
translations.idiomatic: What is to be suspected you do not suspect—upside down and confused, nothing exceeds this; calamity and disorder are close at hand, within the morrow.

sentences.zh: 宜及今幡然改過，整聖駕，謁兩宮，以交父子之歡，則四夷向風，天下慕義矣。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty should now suddenly turn and reform faults, put in order the sacred carriage, and visit the two palaces to exchange the joy between father and son—then the four barbarians will turn to the wind and all under Heaven will admire righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: You should now suddenly turn and reform your faults, put in order the imperial carriage, and visit the two palaces to exchange the joy between father and son—then the four barbarians will turn to you and all under Heaven will admire your righteousness."

sentences.zh: 會壽皇不豫，中外憂危，裳抗聲諫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shouhuang fell ill, within and without all were anxious and fearful; Chang remonstrated in a loud voice.
translations.idiomatic: When the retired emperor fell ill, within and without all were anxious and fearful; Chang remonstrated in a loud voice.

sentences.zh: 上起入宮，裳挽其裾隨之至宮門，揮涕而出。

translations.literal: The sovereign rose and entered the palace; Chang seized his robe and followed him to the palace gate, then waved away his tears and departed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rose and entered the palace; Chang seized his robe and followed him to the palace gate, then wiped away his tears and departed.

sentences.zh: 乃連章請外，謂：「臣職有三：曰待制，曰侍講，曰翊善。

translations.literal: Thereupon he submitted successive memorials requesting an outside post, saying: "Your servant's duties are three: awaiting edict, lecturer-in-waiting, and companion.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he submitted successive memorials requesting an outside post, saying: "My duties are three: awaiting edict, lecturer-in-waiting, and companion.

sentences.zh: 今使供待制之職乎？

translations.literal: If I am now to fulfill the duty of awaiting edict?
translations.idiomatic: If I am now to fulfill the duty of awaiting edict?

sentences.zh: 則當日夕求對以救主失，今不過宮，有虧子道，前後三諫而不加聽，是待制之職可廢也。

translations.literal: then I should day and night seek audience to remedy the sovereign's faults; now Your Majesty does not visit the palace, falling short in the way of a son—three remonstrances before and after without being heeded—the duty of awaiting edict may be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Then I should day and night seek audience to remedy your faults; now you do not visit the palace, falling short in the way of a son—three remonstrances without being heeded—the duty of awaiting edict may be abolished.

sentences.zh: 將使供侍講之職乎？

translations.literal: If I am to fulfill the duty of lecturer-in-waiting?
translations.idiomatic: If I am to fulfill the duty of lecturer-in-waiting?

sentences.zh: 則當引經援古，勸君以孝，今不問安，不視疾，大義已喪，復講何書乎？

translations.literal: then I should cite the classics and draw on antiquity to urge the ruler with filial piety; now without inquiring after well-being, without visiting in illness, the great principle is already lost—what book is there left to lecture?
translations.idiomatic: Then I should cite the classics and draw on antiquity to urge you with filial piety; now without inquiring after your father's well-being, without visiting him in illness, the great principle is already lost—what book is there left to lecture?

sentences.zh: 是侍講之職可廢也。

translations.literal: The duty of lecturer-in-waiting may be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The duty of lecturer-in-waiting may be abolished.

sentences.zh: 將使供翊善之職乎？

translations.literal: If I am to fulfill the duty of companion?
translations.idiomatic: If I am to fulfill the duty of companion?

sentences.zh: 當究義理，教皇子以孝，陛下不能以孝事壽皇，臣將何說以勸皇子乎？

translations.literal: I should investigate principle and teach the prince filial piety; Your Majesty cannot serve Emperor Shouhuang with filial piety—with what words can your servant urge the prince?
translations.idiomatic: I should investigate principle and teach the prince filial piety; you cannot serve the retired emperor with filial piety—with what words can I urge the prince?

sentences.zh: 是翊善之職可廢也。」

translations.literal: The duty of companion may be abolished."
translations.idiomatic: The duty of companion may be abolished."

sentences.zh: 因出關待命。

translations.literal: With that, he left through the pass and awaited orders.
translations.idiomatic: With that, he left through the pass and awaited further orders.

sentences.zh: 及聞壽皇遺詔，乃亟入臨。

translations.literal: When he heard the retired Emperor Shouhuang's death edict, he hurried in to take part in the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Upon hearing the retired emperor Shouhuang's final edict, he rushed to the palace to mourn.

sentences.zh: 寧宗即位，裳病不能朝。

translations.literal: When Ningzong ascended the throne, Chang was ill and could not attend court.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ningzong took the throne, Huang Chang was too ill to attend court.

sentences.zh: 改禮部尚書，尋兼侍讀。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Rites, and soon also made Concurrent Reader.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Minister of Rites and soon also made a concurrent palace reader.

sentences.zh: 力疾入謝，奏曰：

translations.literal: Forcing himself despite his illness, he entered to express thanks and memorialized, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Summoning what strength he had left, he went in to offer thanks and submitted a memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 「孔子曰：『有始有卒者，其惟聖人乎？』

translations.literal: "Confucius said: 'Only the sage completes what he begins, does he not?'
translations.idiomatic: "Confucius said: 'Only the sage truly finishes what he starts, does he not?'

sentences.zh: 又《詩》曰：『靡不有初，鮮克有終。』

translations.literal: The Odes also says: 'Nothing lacks a beginning; few bring things to completion.'
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Odes also says: 'Nothing is without a beginning, yet few see things through to the end.'

sentences.zh: 所謂『有始有卒』者，由其持心之一也；

translations.literal: What is meant by 'completing what one begins' is due to the singleness of one's resolve;
translations.idiomatic: What we call 'seeing things through' comes from holding fast to a single purpose;

sentences.zh: 所謂『鮮克有終』者，由其持心之不一也。

translations.literal: what is meant by 'few bring things to completion' is due to the inconsistency of one's resolve.
translations.idiomatic: what we call 'failing to finish' comes from a heart that does not hold steady.

sentences.zh: 陛下今日初政固善矣，能保他日常如此乎？

translations.literal: Your Majesty's initial policies today are indeed good — can you guarantee they will remain so in days to come?
translations.idiomatic: Your opening policies today are indeed admirable — but can you ensure they will stay this way in the years ahead?

sentences.zh: 請略舉已行之事論之。

translations.literal: Allow me briefly to take what has already been done as examples for discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Allow me to take what you have already done and discuss it briefly.

sentences.zh: 陛下初理萬機，委任大臣，此正得人君持要之道。
