translations.literal: Your Majesty, at the outset of handling the myriad affairs of state, has entrusted great ministers — this is precisely the way a ruler should grasp what is essential.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset of your reign you have taken up the myriad affairs of state and entrusted them to senior ministers — this is exactly how a ruler should hold to what matters most.

sentences.zh: 使大臣得人，常如今日，則陛下雖終身守之可也。

translations.literal: If the great ministers appointed are worthy men and this remains as it is today, then Your Majesty could maintain this for a lifetime.
translations.idiomatic: If the ministers you appoint are the right men and this practice endures as it does today, you could uphold it for your whole reign.

sentences.zh: 臣恐數年之後，亦欲出意作為，躬親聽斷，左右迎合，因謂陛下事決外庭，權不歸上，陛下能不咈然於心乎？

translations.literal: I fear that in a few years Your Majesty will also wish to act on your own initiative, personally hearing and deciding cases; those around you will flatter you, saying that affairs are decided in the outer court and authority does not return to the sovereign — could Your Majesty fail to feel resentment in your heart?
translations.idiomatic: I fear that in a few years you may wish to strike out on your own, personally hearing and deciding every matter. Those around you will pander to you, saying that decisions are made outside the throne room and that power no longer rests with the emperor — could you fail to feel stung by that?

sentences.zh: 臣恐是時委任大臣，不能如今日之專矣。

translations.literal: I fear that at that time the entrusting of great ministers will no longer be as full and exclusive as it is today.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that by then your delegation of authority to senior ministers will no longer be as complete as it is today.

sentences.zh: 夫以萬機之眾，非一人所能酬酢，苟不委任大臣，則必借助左右，小人得志，陰竊主權，引用邪黨，其為禍患，何所不至，臣之所憂者一也。

translations.literal: Now the multitude of state affairs is more than one man can respond to; if great ministers are not entrusted, one must rely on those at one's side. When petty men get their way, they secretly usurp sovereign authority, bring in wicked factions — what calamity could not follow? This is the first thing your servant fears.
translations.idiomatic: The affairs of state are too numerous for one man to handle alone. If you do not entrust them to senior ministers, you will inevitably rely on those at your side. Petty men will prevail, secretly seize authority, and bring in corrupt factions — and from there, what disaster might not follow? This is my first concern.

sentences.zh: 陛下獎用臺諫，言無不聽，此正得祖宗設官之意。

translations.literal: Your Majesty encourages and employs censors and remonstrators, and no word of theirs goes unheeded — this is precisely in accord with the intent of our ancestors in establishing these offices.
translations.idiomatic: You encourage and employ censors and remonstrators, and heed their every word — this is exactly what our ancestors intended when they created these offices.

sentences.zh: 使臺諫得人，常如今日，則陛下終身守之亦可也。

translations.literal: If the censors and remonstrators appointed are worthy men and this remains as it is today, then Your Majesty could uphold this for a lifetime as well.
translations.idiomatic: If the censors and remonstrators you appoint are the right men and this practice continues as it does today, you could uphold it for your whole reign.

sentences.zh: 然臣恐自今以往，臺諫之言日關聖聽，或斥小人之過，使陛下欲用之而不能，或暴近習之罪，使陛下欲親之而不可。

translations.literal: Yet I fear that from now on the words of censors and remonstrators will daily reach Your Majesty's ears — some exposing the faults of petty men so that Your Majesty wishes to employ them but cannot, others revealing the crimes of close attendants so that Your Majesty wishes to keep them near but may not.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I fear that from now on their words will reach your ears every day — some exposing the faults of petty men so that you wish to employ them but cannot, others revealing the crimes of close attendants so that you wish to keep them near but dare not.

sentences.zh: 逆耳之言，不能無厭，左右迎合，因謂陛下獎用臺諫，欲聞讜論，而其流弊，致使人主不能自由，陛下能不咈然於心乎？

translations.literal: Words that grate on the ear cannot but eventually weary one; those around you will flatter you, saying that Your Majesty encourages censors and remonstrators because you wish to hear honest counsel, yet the abuse of this practice makes the ruler unable to act freely — could Your Majesty fail to feel resentment in your heart?
translations.idiomatic: Unpleasant truths cannot but eventually grow tiresome. Those around you will pander to you, saying that you encourage censors because you wish to hear honest counsel, yet that the practice has gone so far as to leave the ruler no freedom of action — could you fail to feel stung by that?

sentences.zh: 臣恐是時獎用臺諫，不能如今日之重矣。

translations.literal: I fear that at that time the encouragement and employment of censors and remonstrators will no longer carry the weight it does today.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that by then your encouragement of censors and remonstrators will no longer carry the weight it does today.

sentences.zh: 夫朝廷所恃以分別善惡者，專在臺諫，陛下苟厭其多言，則為臺諫者，將咋舌閉口，無所論列。

translations.literal: The court relies on censors and remonstrators alone to distinguish good from evil; if Your Majesty grows weary of their many words, then those who serve as censors and remonstrators will bite their tongues and close their mouths, with nothing left to set forth.
translations.idiomatic: The court relies on censors and remonstrators alone to distinguish right from wrong. If you grow weary of their many words, they will bite their tongues and fall silent, with nothing left to say.

sentences.zh: 君子日退，小人日進，而天下亂矣，臣之所憂者二也。

translations.literal: Men of worth will daily retreat while petty men daily advance, and the realm will fall into disorder — this is the second thing your servant fears.
translations.idiomatic: Men of worth will retreat day by day while petty men advance, and the realm will fall into disorder — this is my second concern.

sentences.zh: 二事，朝廷之大者。

translations.literal: These two matters are great affairs of the court.
translations.idiomatic: These two matters are the greatest concerns of the court.

sentences.zh: 又以三事之切于陛下之身言之：曰篤於孝愛，勤于學問，薄於嗜好。

translations.literal: I will also speak of three matters that bear directly on Your Majesty's person: being deep in filial love, diligent in study, and sparing in personal indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: I will also speak of three matters that bear directly on you personally: deep filial devotion, diligent study, and restraint in personal indulgence.

sentences.zh: 陛下今皆行之矣，未知數年之後，能保常如今日乎？

translations.literal: Your Majesty now practices all of these — but can you guarantee that in a few years they will remain as they are today?
translations.idiomatic: You practice all of these today — but can you ensure that in a few years they will still be as they are now?

sentences.zh: 又引魏徵十漸以為戒，懇懇數千言。

translations.literal: He also cited Wei Zheng's Ten Gradual Changes as a warning, earnestly setting forth several thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: He also cited Wei Zheng's Ten Gradual Changes as a warning, earnestly setting forth several thousand words of counsel.

sentences.zh: 又奏言：「陛下近日所為頗異前日，除授之際，大臣多有不知，臣聞之憂甚而病劇。」

translations.literal: He further memorialized: "Your Majesty's recent conduct differs considerably from what came before; at the time of appointments and dismissals, many great ministers did not know — when your servant heard of this, his worry was deep and his illness grew worse."
translations.idiomatic: He further submitted: "Your recent conduct differs markedly from what came before. At the time of appointments and dismissals, many senior ministers were kept in the dark. When I heard of this, my worry deepened and my illness grew worse."

sentences.zh: 蓋是時韓侂胄已潛弄威柄，而宰相趙汝愚未之覺，故裳先事言之。

translations.literal: For at that time Han Tuozhou was already secretly wielding power, while the chief councilor Zhao Ruyu had not yet perceived it — therefore Chang spoke out beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: For at that time Han Tuozhou was already secretly wielding power, while Chief Councilor Zhao Ruyu had not yet perceived it — so Huang Chang spoke out before the crisis arrived.

sentences.zh: 及疾革，時時獨語，曰：「五年之功，無使一日壞之，度吾已不可為，後之君子必有能任其責者。」

translations.literal: When his illness reached its crisis, he would from time to time speak alone, saying: "Five years of achievement — let not a single day ruin it. I reckon I can no longer act; later men of worth will surely be able to bear this responsibility."
translations.idiomatic: When his illness reached its final stage, he would murmur to himself from time to time: "Five years of achievement — do not let a single day undo it. I reckon I can do no more; later men of worth will surely be able to bear this responsibility."

sentences.zh: 遂口占遺表而卒，年四十九。

translations.literal: Thereupon he orally composed his final memorial and died, at the age of forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He then dictated his final memorial and died, at the age of forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 上聞之驚悼，贈資政殿學士。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it, he was startled and grieved, and posthumously granted him the title of Academician of the Hall for Assistance in Governance.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of it, he was shocked and grieved, and posthumously granted him the title of Academician of the Hall for Assistance in Governance.

sentences.zh: 裳為人簡易端純，每講讀，隨事納忠，上援古義，下揆人情，氣平而辭切，事該而理盡。

translations.literal: Chang as a man was simple, upright, and pure. Whenever he lectured, he offered loyal counsel as occasion arose — drawing on ancient principles above and gauging human feelings below, his tone was calm yet his words incisive, his matters comprehensive and his reasoning exhaustive.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chang was a plain, upright, and sincere man. Whenever he lectured, he offered loyal counsel as the occasion arose — drawing on ancient principles and gauging human feeling, his tone was calm yet his words sharp, his coverage broad and his reasoning thorough.

sentences.zh: 篤于孝友，與人言傾盡底蘊。

translations.literal: Deep in filial piety and brotherly affection, in speaking with others he fully revealed the depths of his mind.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply devoted in filial piety and brotherly affection, he spoke with others with complete openness.

sentences.zh: 恥一書不讀，一物不知。

translations.literal: He was ashamed to leave a single book unread or a single thing unknown.
translations.idiomatic: He was ashamed to leave any book unread or any subject unknown.

sentences.zh: 推賢樂善，出乎天性。

translations.literal: Promoting the worthy and delighting in goodness came from his inborn nature.
translations.idiomatic: Promoting the worthy and delighting in goodness came naturally to him.

sentences.zh: 所為文，明白條達。

translations.literal: The writings he produced were clear and orderly.
translations.idiomatic: His writings were clear, orderly, and lucid.

sentences.zh: 有《王府春秋講義》及《兼山集》，論天人之理，性命之源，皆足以發明伊、洛之旨。

translations.literal: He had the Exposition of the Spring and Autumn for the Princely Household and the Collected Works of Jianshan; in discussing the principles of Heaven and man and the sources of nature and destiny, both were sufficient to elucidate the teachings of the Yi and Luo schools.
translations.idiomatic: He authored the Exposition of the Spring and Autumn for the Princely Household and the Collected Works of Jianshan. In discussing the principles of Heaven and man and the sources of human nature and destiny, both works were sufficient to elucidate the teachings of the Cheng brothers.

sentences.zh: 嘗與其鄉人陳平父兄弟講學，平父，張栻之門人也，師友淵源，蓋有自來云。

translations.literal: He once lectured on learning with his fellow townsman Chen Pingfu and his brothers. Pingfu was a disciple of Zhang Shi — the deep source of his teachers and friends had its origin from of old, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: He once lectured on learning with his fellow townsman Chen Pingfu and his brothers. Pingfu was a disciple of Zhang Shi — the deep lineage of his teachers and friends, it is said, had long been established.

sentences.zh: 嘉定中，諡「忠文」。

translations.literal: In the Jiading era, he was given the posthumous title "Loyal and Literary."
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiading era, he was given the posthumous title "Loyal and Literary."

sentences.zh: 子：瑾，大宗正丞兼刑部郎官。

translations.literal: His son: Jin, Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan concurrently Ministerial Assistant in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jin served as Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan and concurrently as a ministerial assistant in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 孫：子敏，刑部郎官。

translations.literal: His grandson: Zimin, Ministerial Assistant in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Zimin served as a ministerial assistant in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 羅點，字春伯，撫州崇仁人。

translations.literal: Luo Dian, styled Chunbo, was a native of Chongren in Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Dian, styled Chunbo, was a native of Chongren in Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 六歲能文。

translations.literal: At the age of six he could compose literary pieces.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of six he could already write essays.

sentences.zh: 登淳熙三年進士第，授定江節度推官。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the third year of the Chunxi era and was appointed military judicial officer of the Dingjiang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the third year of the Chunxi era and was appointed military judicial officer of the Dingjiang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 累遷校書郎兼國史院編修官。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Proofreader concurrently Compiler at the National History Institute.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to Proofreader and concurrent compiler at the National History Institute.

sentences.zh: 歲旱，詔求言，點上封事，謂：「今時姦諛日甚，議論凡陋。

translations.literal: In a year of drought, an edict sought remonstrance; Dian submitted a sealed memorial, saying: "At present flattery and sycophancy grow daily, while discussion is vulgar and shallow.
translations.idiomatic: During a drought year, the throne issued an edict soliciting remonstrance. Dian submitted a sealed memorial, saying: "Flattery and sycophancy grow worse by the day, while public discussion grows ever more shallow.

sentences.zh: 無所可否，則曰得體；

translations.literal: If one neither approves nor disapproves, they say one is 'appropriate';
translations.idiomatic: If one neither approves nor disapproves, they call it 'knowing one's place';

sentences.zh: 與世浮沈，則曰有量；

translations.literal: if one drifts with the world, they say one has 'breadth';
translations.idiomatic: if one drifts with the tide, they call it 'magnanimity';

sentences.zh: 眾皆默，己獨言，則曰沽名；

translations.literal: if all are silent and one alone speaks, they say one is 'seeking a name';
translations.idiomatic: if all are silent and one alone speaks out, they call it 'seeking fame';

sentences.zh: 眾皆濁，己獨清，則曰立異。

translations.literal: if all are turbid and one alone is clear, they say one is 'making oneself different.'
translations.idiomatic: if all are corrupt and one alone stands clear, they call it 'being contrarian.'

sentences.zh: 此風不革，陛下雖欲大有為於天下，未見其可也。

translations.literal: If this custom is not reformed, even though Your Majesty wishes to accomplish great things under Heaven, I do not see how it can be done.
translations.idiomatic: If this custom is not reformed, even if you wish to accomplish great things for the realm, I do not see how it can be done.

sentences.zh: 自旱暵為虐，陛下禱群祠，赦有罪，曾不足以感動。

translations.literal: Since the drought's ravages began, Your Majesty has prayed at all shrines and pardoned the guilty — yet these were not enough to move Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Since the drought began its ravages, you have prayed at every shrine and pardoned the guilty — yet none of this was enough to move Heaven.

sentences.zh: 及朝求讜言，夕得甘雨，天心所示，昭然不誣。

translations.literal: Yet when remonstrance was sought in the morning, sweet rain fell by evening — what Heaven's heart revealed was plainly no deception.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when honest counsel was sought in the morning, sweet rain fell by evening — Heaven's response was plainly no deception.

sentences.zh: 獨不知陛下之求言，果欲用之否乎？

translations.literal: I alone do not know whether Your Majesty, in seeking remonstrance, truly intends to use it or not.
translations.idiomatic: I wonder alone whether you truly intend to act on the counsel you solicit.

sentences.zh: 如欲用之，則願以所上封事，反覆詳熟，當者審而後行，疑者諮而後決，如此則治象日著，而亂萌自消矣。」

translations.literal: If you wish to use it, then I hope Your Majesty will go over the sealed memorials submitted, examining them repeatedly and thoroughly — what is fitting, consider carefully before acting; what is doubtful, consult before deciding. In this way the signs of good governance will daily become clear, and the seeds of disorder will naturally disappear."
translations.idiomatic: If you truly wish to use it, then go over the sealed memorials submitted, examining them carefully — what is fitting, consider thoroughly before acting; what is doubtful, consult before deciding. In this way the signs of good governance will grow clearer day by day, and the seeds of disorder will naturally wither away."

sentences.zh: 遷秘書郎兼皇太子宮小學教授。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Secretary concurrently Instructor at the Crown Prince's Palace Primary School.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Secretary and concurrent instructor at the crown prince's palace primary school.

sentences.zh: 寧宗時以皇孫封英國公，點兼教授，入講至晡時不輟，左右請少憩，點曰：「國公務學不休，奈何止之。」

translations.literal: During Ningzong's reign the imperial grandson was enfeoffed as Duke of Ying; Dian served concurrently as instructor. He entered to lecture and did not cease until dusk; those at the prince's side asked that he rest awhile. Dian said: "The Duke is devoted to learning without pause — how can we stop him?"
translations.idiomatic: During Ningzong's reign the imperial grandson was enfeoffed as Duke of Ying, and Dian served as his concurrent instructor. He lectured without stopping until dusk. Attendants asked that he rest awhile. Dian said: "The duke is devoted to his studies without pause — how can we stop him?"

sentences.zh: 又摭古事勸戒，為《鑒古錄》以進。

translations.literal: He also gathered ancient examples for admonition and compiled the Record for Reflecting on Antiquity, which he presented to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He also gathered ancient examples for admonition and compiled the Record for Reflecting on Antiquity, which he presented to the throne.

sentences.zh: 高宗崩，孝宗在諒暗，皇太子參決庶務，點時以戶部員外郎兼太子侍講，出使浙右，遷起居舍人，改太常少卿兼侍立修注官，被命使金告登寶位。

translations.literal: When Gaozong died, Xiaozong was in mourning seclusion and the crown prince participated in deciding routine affairs. Dian at the time was Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue concurrently Lecturer to the Crown Prince; he went on mission to the right of Zhe, was promoted to Diarist, was changed to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices concurrently Attending Compiler, and was ordered on embassy to Jin to announce the accession to the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong died, Xiaozong was in mourning seclusion and the crown prince began participating in routine affairs of state. Dian was then a vice director in the Ministry of Revenue and concurrent lecturer to the crown prince. He went on mission to Zhejiang, was promoted to diarist, then appointed vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and concurrent attending compiler, and was ordered on embassy to Jin to announce Ningzong's accession to the throne.

sentences.zh: 會金有國喪，迫點易金帶，點曰：「登位吉事也，必以吉服從事。

translations.literal: It happened that Jin was in national mourning, and they pressed Dian to change to a mourning sash. Dian said: "Accession to the throne is an auspicious affair — one must conduct it in auspicious dress.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Jin was in national mourning, and they pressed Dian to change to mourning attire. Dian said: "Accession to the throne is an auspicious affair — one must conduct it in festive dress.

sentences.zh: 有死而已，帶不可易。」

translations.literal: I would die before I would change the sash."
translations.idiomatic: I would die before I would change my sash."

sentences.zh: 又詰點不當稱「寶位」，點曰：「聖人大寶曰位，不加『寶」字，何以別至尊。」

translations.literal: They again questioned whether Dian ought to use the term "imperial throne." Dian said: "The great treasure of the sage is the throne — if one does not add the character 'treasure,' how is the utmost honor to be distinguished?"
translations.idiomatic: They again challenged his use of the term "imperial throne." Dian said: "The great treasure of the sage is the throne — if one does not add the character 'treasure,' how is the utmost honor to be distinguished?"

sentences.zh: 金人不能奪。

translations.literal: The men of Jin could not prevail over him.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin envoys could not prevail over him.

sentences.zh: 上嘗謂點：「卿舊為宮僚，非他人比，有所欲言，毋憚啟告。」

translations.literal: The emperor once said to Dian: "You formerly served in the palace staff — you are not to be compared with others. If there is anything you wish to say, do not hesitate to speak openly."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once said to Dian: "You formerly served in the palace staff — you are not like others. If there is anything you wish to say, do not hesitate to speak openly."

sentences.zh: 點言：「君子得志常少，小人得志常多。

translations.literal: Dian said: "Men of worth who attain their aims are often few; petty men who attain their aims are often many.
translations.idiomatic: Dian said: "Men of worth who attain their aims are often few; petty men who attain their aims are often many.

sentences.zh: 蓋君子志在天下國家，而不在一己，行必直道，言必正論，往往不忤人主，則忤貴近，不忤當路，則忤時俗。

translations.literal: This is because men of worth set their hearts on the realm and the state, not on themselves alone. In conduct they must follow the straight path; in speech they must offer upright discourse. Often they do not offend the ruler, yet they offend the noble and the close; they do not offend those in power, yet they offend the customs of the age.
translations.idiomatic: This is because men of worth set their hearts on the realm and the state, not on themselves alone. They follow the straight path in conduct and offer upright counsel in speech. Often they do not offend the ruler, yet they offend the powerful and the well-connected; they do not offend those in office, yet they offend the customs of the age.

sentences.zh: 小人志在一己，而不在天下國家，所行所言，皆取悅之道。

translations.literal: Petty men set their hearts on themselves alone, not on the realm and the state; in all they do and say, they follow the path of pleasing others.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men set their hearts on themselves alone, not on the realm and the state. In all they do and say, they follow the path of pleasing others.

sentences.zh: 用其所以取忤者，其得志鮮矣；

translations.literal: Employ what makes them give offense, and few of them will attain their aims;
translations.idiomatic: Employ those whose ways give offense, and few of them will attain their aims;

sentences.zh: 用其所以取悅者，其不得志亦鮮矣。

translations.literal: employ what makes them pleasing, and few of them will fail to attain their aims.
translations.idiomatic: employ those whose ways are pleasing, and few of them will fail to attain their aims.

sentences.zh: 若昔明主，念君子之難進，則極所以主張而覆護之；

translations.literal: When enlightened rulers of old considered how hard it was for men of worth to advance, they did all they could to support and protect them;
translations.idiomatic: When enlightened rulers of old saw how hard it was for men of worth to advance, they did all they could to support and protect them;

sentences.zh: 念小人之難退，則盡所以燭察而隄防之。」

translations.literal: considering how hard it was for petty men to withdraw, they did all they could to scrutinize and guard against them."
translations.idiomatic: and seeing how hard it was for petty men to withdraw, they did all they could to scrutinize and guard against them."

sentences.zh: 皇子嘉王年及弱冠，點言：「此正親師友、進德業之時，宜擇端良忠直之士，參侍燕間。」

translations.literal: When the prince, Prince Ji, reached the age of capping, Dian said: "This is precisely the time to be close to teachers and friends and advance in virtue and achievement. Worthy, upright, and loyal men should be chosen to attend him in his leisure hours."
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Ji reached the age of capping, Dian said: "This is precisely the time to draw close to teachers and friends and advance in virtue and learning. Upright, loyal men of good character should be chosen to attend him in his leisure hours."

sentences.zh: 遂除黃裳為翊善。

translations.literal: Thereupon Huang Chang was appointed Companion.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Huang Chang was appointed companion to the prince.

sentences.zh: 又言：「人主憂勤，則臣下協心；

translations.literal: He also said: "When the ruler is anxious and diligent, then his ministers unite in purpose;
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "When the ruler is anxious and diligent, his ministers unite in purpose;

sentences.zh: 人主偷安，則臣下解體。

translations.literal: when the ruler seeks ease, then his ministers fall apart.
translations.idiomatic: when the ruler seeks ease, his ministers fall apart.

sentences.zh: 今道塗之言，皆謂陛下每旦視朝，勉強聽斷，意不在事。

translations.literal: Now the talk on the roads all says that Your Majesty each morning holds court, forcing himself to hear and decide cases, with his mind not on the affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Now the talk on the roads says that each morning you hold court only with effort, hearing and deciding cases with your mind not on the affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 宰執奏陳，備禮應答，侍從庶僚，備禮登對，而宮中燕游之樂，錫齎奢侈之費，已騰於眾口。

translations.literal: The chief councilors memorialize and report, going through the forms in reply; attendants and various officials go through the forms in audience — yet the pleasures of feasting and roaming in the palace, and the lavish costs of imperial gifts, have already spread on every tongue.
translations.idiomatic: The chief councilors memorialize and report, going through the motions in reply; attendants and various officials go through the motions in audience — yet the pleasures of feasting and roaming in the palace, and the lavish costs of imperial gifts, are already on everyone's lips.

sentences.zh: 強敵對境，此聲豈可出哉！」

translations.literal: With a powerful enemy on the border, how can such talk be allowed to arise!"
translations.idiomatic: With a powerful enemy on the border, how can such talk be allowed to spread!"

sentences.zh: 紹熙三年十一月日長至，車駕將朝賀重華宮，既而中輟。

translations.literal: On the winter solstice in the eleventh month of the third year of the Shaoxi era, the imperial carriage was about to proceed to Chonghua Palace for the congratulatory audience, but was then halted midway.
translations.idiomatic: On the winter solstice in the eleventh month of the third year of the Shaoxi era, the imperial carriage was about to proceed to Chonghua Palace for the congratulatory audience, but was halted midway.

sentences.zh: 點言：「自天子達庶人，節序拜親，無有闕者，三綱五常，所係甚大，不當以為常事而忽之。」

translations.literal: Dian said: "From the Son of Heaven down to the common people, at each seasonal occasion one pays respects to one's parents — none may be omitted. The Three Bonds and Five Constants are greatly involved; this should not be treated as an ordinary matter and neglected."
translations.idiomatic: Dian said: "From the Son of Heaven down to the common people, at each seasonal occasion one pays respects to one's parents — none may be omitted. The Three Bonds and Five Constants are at stake; this should not be treated as routine and neglected."

sentences.zh: 上過宮意未決，點奏：「陛下已涓日過宮，壽皇必引領以俟陛下。

translations.literal: The emperor's intention to visit the palace was still unsettled. Dian memorialized: "Your Majesty has already chosen a day to visit the palace — Emperor Shouhuang must be craning his neck awaiting Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's intention to visit the palace was still unsettled. Dian memorialized: "You have already chosen a day to visit the palace — the retired emperor Shouhuang must be waiting eagerly for you.

sentences.zh: 常人于朋友且不可以無信，況人主之事親乎？

translations.literal: Even an ordinary person cannot be without good faith toward friends — how much more so the ruler in serving his parent?
translations.idiomatic: Even an ordinary person cannot be faithless toward friends — how much more so the ruler in serving his parent?

sentences.zh: 今陛下久闕溫凊，壽皇欲見不可得，萬一憂思感疾，陛下將何以自解於天下？」

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty has long neglected inquiries after warmth and coolness; Emperor Shouhuang wishes to see you but cannot. If by chance worry and grief should bring on illness, how will Your Majesty explain yourself to the realm?"
translations.idiomatic: You have long neglected to inquire after your father's well-being; the retired emperor wishes to see you but cannot. If worry and grief should bring on illness, how will you explain yourself to the realm?"

sentences.zh: 嘗召對便殿，點言：「近者中外相傳，或謂陛下內有所制，不能遽出，溺於酒色，不恤政事，果有之乎？」

translations.literal: He was once summoned for audience in the side hall. Dian said: "Recently it is rumored inside and outside the court that Your Majesty is inwardly constrained, unable to go out promptly, drowning in wine and women, and uncaring of state affairs — is this truly so?"
translations.idiomatic: He was once summoned for audience in the side hall. Dian said: "Recently it is rumored inside and outside the court that you are inwardly constrained, unable to go out promptly, drowning in wine and women, and uncaring of state affairs — is this truly so?"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「無是。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "It is not so."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "It is not so."

sentences.zh: 點曰：「臣固知之。

translations.literal: Dian said: "Your servant knew as much.
translations.idiomatic: Dian said: "I knew as much.

sentences.zh: 竊意宮禁間或有攖拂之事，姑以酒自遣耳。

translations.literal: I privately surmise that within the palace there may be matters that vex and disturb you, and that for the moment you seek relief in wine.
translations.idiomatic: I privately surmise that within the palace there may be matters that vex and disturb you, and that for the moment you seek relief in wine.

sentences.zh: 夫閭閻匹夫，處閨門逆境，容有縱酒自放者。

translations.literal: A common man in his lane, facing adversity within his household, may perhaps indulge in wine and abandon restraint.
translations.idiomatic: A common man in his lane, facing adversity within his household, may perhaps indulge in wine and abandon restraint.

sentences.zh: 人主宰制天下，此心如青天白日，當風雨雷電既霽之餘，湛然虛明，豈容復有纖芥停留哉？」

translations.literal: The ruler who governs the realm — his heart should be like the blue sky and bright sun, like the clear emptiness and brightness after wind, rain, thunder, and lightning have passed — how could the slightest speck be allowed to remain?"
translations.idiomatic: The ruler who governs the realm — his heart should be like the clear sky and bright sun, like the luminous clarity after wind, rain, thunder, and lightning have passed — how could the slightest speck be allowed to remain?"

sentences.zh: 上猶未過宮。

translations.literal: The emperor still had not visited the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still had not visited the palace.

sentences.zh: 點又奏：「竊聞嘉王生朝，稱壽禁中，以報劬勞之德，父子歡洽，寧不動心，上念兩宮延望之意。」

translations.literal: Dian again memorialized: "I have privately heard that on Prince Ji's birthday, congratulations were held within the palace to repay the virtue of his parents' toil — father and son rejoicing together. Could this fail to move the heart and turn the mind to the longing of both palaces?"
translations.idiomatic: Dian again memorialized: "I have privately heard that on Prince Ji's birthday, congratulations were held within the palace to honor his parents' toil — father and son rejoicing together. Could this fail to move your heart and turn your mind to the longing of both palaces?"

sentences.zh: 十一月，點以言不見聽，求去，不許。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, because his words went unheeded, Dian requested dismissal, but was not permitted to leave.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, because his words went unheeded, Dian requested dismissal, but was not permitted to leave.

sentences.zh: 十二月，試兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, he was appointed acting Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, he was appointed acting Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 五年四月，上將幸玉津園，點請先過重華，又奏曰：「陛下為壽皇子，四十餘年一無閑言，止緣初郊違豫，壽皇嘗至南內督過，左右之人自此讒間，遂生憂疑。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fifth year, the emperor was about to visit the Jade Ford Garden. Dian asked that he first visit Chonghua Palace, and again memorialized: "Your Majesty, as son to Emperor Shouhuang, for more than forty years had not a word of reproach — it was only because at the first suburban sacrifice you were unwell that Emperor Shouhuang once came to the Southern Palace to urge you to visit. From then on, those around you slandered and estranged you, and worry and suspicion arose.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fifth year, the emperor was about to visit the Jade Ford Garden. Dian asked that he first visit Chonghua Palace, and again memorialized: "As son to the retired emperor Shouhuang, for more than forty years you had not a word of reproach against you — it was only because at the first suburban sacrifice you were unwell that Shouhuang once came to the Southern Palace to urge you to visit. From then on, those around you slandered and estranged you, and worry and suspicion arose.

sentences.zh: 以臣觀之，壽皇與天下相忘久矣。

translations.literal: In your servant's view, Emperor Shouhuang and the realm have long since forgotten each other.
translations.idiomatic: In my view, the retired emperor Shouhuang and the realm have long since put such matters out of mind.

sentences.zh: 今大臣同心輔政，百執事奉法循理，宗室、戚里、三軍、萬姓皆無貳志，設有離間，誅之不疑。

translations.literal: Now the great ministers are of one mind in assisting governance; the hundred officials follow law and principle; the imperial clan, consort kin, the three armies, and the myriad people all have no divided hearts. If anyone should seek to estrange you, execute him without hesitation.
translations.idiomatic: Now the senior ministers are of one mind in assisting governance; the hundred officials follow law and principle; the imperial clan, consort kin, the three armies, and the myriad people all stand united. If anyone seeks to estrange you, execute him without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 乃若深居不出，久虧子道，眾口謗讟，禍患將作，不可以不慮。」

translations.literal: Yet if you deeply seclude yourself and do not go out, long falling short in the way of a son, the mouths of the multitude will slander and revile — calamity is about to arise, and this cannot be left unconsidered."
translations.idiomatic: Yet if you deeply seclude yourself and do not go out, long falling short in the way of a son, the mouths of the multitude will slander and revile you — calamity is about to arise, and this cannot be left unconsidered."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿等可為朕調護之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You may mediate and reconcile this for Us."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "You may mediate and reconcile this for me."

sentences.zh: 黃裳對曰：「父子之親，何俟調護？」

translations.literal: Huang Chang replied: "The closeness between father and son — what need is there for mediation?"
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chang replied: "The bond between father and son — what need is there for mediation?"

sentences.zh: 點曰：「陛下一出，即當釋然。」

translations.literal: Dian said: "Once Your Majesty goes out once, you will immediately feel relieved."
translations.idiomatic: Dian said: "Once you go out, you will immediately feel at ease."

sentences.zh: 上猶未行。

translations.literal: The emperor still did not go.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still did not go.

sentences.zh: 點乃率講官言之，上曰：「朕心未嘗不思壽皇。」

translations.literal: Dian then led the lecturing officials in speaking of it. The emperor said: "My heart has never failed to think of Emperor Shouhuang."
translations.idiomatic: Dian then had the lecturing officials speak on the matter together. The emperor said: "My heart has never ceased to turn to the retired emperor Shouhuang."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陛下久闕定省，雖有此心，何以自白乎？」

translations.literal: He replied: "Your Majesty has long neglected the duties of attendance and inquiry — though you have this heart, how can you make it clear to others?"
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "You have long neglected to attend and inquire after your father — though you hold this sentiment in your heart, how can you make it known?"

sentences.zh: 及壽皇不豫，點又隨宰執班進諫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shouhuang fell ill, Dian again followed the chief ministers' ranks to advance remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouhuang fell ill, Dian again joined the chief ministers in presenting remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 閤門吏止之，點叱之而入。

translations.literal: The gate officer stopped him; Dian rebuked him and entered.
translations.idiomatic: A gate officer barred his way; Dian shouted him down and entered.

sentences.zh: 上拂衣起，宰執引上裾，點亟前泣奏曰：「壽皇疾勢已危，不及今一見，後悔何及。」

translations.literal: The emperor brushed aside his robes and rose. The chief ministers seized his hem. Dian hastened forward and tearfully memorialized: "Emperor Shouhuang's illness is already critical — if you do not see him now, how could you ever not regret it?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor brushed aside his robes and rose. The chief ministers seized his robe. Dian hastened forward and tearfully pleaded: "Shouhuang's illness is already critical — if you do not see him now, regret will come too late."

sentences.zh: 群臣隨上入至福寧殿，內侍闔門，眾慟哭而退。

translations.literal: The assembled ministers followed the emperor in to the Funing Hall; the eunuchs closed the doors, and the crowd wept and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers followed the emperor into the Funing Hall; the eunuchs closed the doors, and the others wept and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 越三日，點隨宰執班起居，詔獨引點入。

translations.literal: Three days later, Dian joined the chief ministers' ranks for the daily audience; an edict summoned Dian alone to enter.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later, Dian attended with the chief ministers for the daily audience; an edict summoned Dian alone into the palace.

sentences.zh: 點奏：「前日迫切獻忠，舉措失禮，陛下赦而不誅，然引裾亦故事也。」

translations.literal: Dian memorialized: "The other day, in my urgent zeal to offer loyal counsel, my conduct was improper in courtesy. Your Majesty pardoned rather than punished — yet holding the emperor's robe is also established precedent."
translations.idiomatic: Dian memorialized: "The other day, in urgent zeal to offer loyal counsel, my conduct breached propriety. You pardoned me instead of punishing me — yet seizing the emperor's robe is also established precedent."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「引裾可也，何得輒入宮禁乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Seizing the robe may be permitted — how could you presumptuously enter the palace precincts?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Seizing the robe may be permitted — but how could you presumptuously enter the palace precincts?"

sentences.zh: 點引辛毗事以謝，且言：「壽皇止有一子，既付神器，惟恐見之不速耳。」

translations.literal: Dian cited the affair of Xin Pi in apology, and added: "Emperor Shouhuang had only one son; having entrusted him with the sacred vessel, he feared only that he might not see him soon enough."
translations.idiomatic: Dian cited the precedent of Xin Pi in apology, and added: "Shouhuang had only one son; having entrusted the throne to him, he feared only that he might not see him soon enough."

sentences.zh: 壽皇崩，點請上奔喪，許而不出，拜遺詔于重華宮。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shouhuang died, Dian asked the emperor to rush to the mourning; permission was granted but he did not go out; he paid respects to the final edict at Chonghua Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouhuang died, Dian urged the emperor to rush to the mourning hall; permission was granted but he still did not go; he paid respects to the final edict at Chonghua Palace.

sentences.zh: 前後與侍從列奏諫請帝過宮者凡三十五疏，自上奏者又十六章，而奏疏重華，上書嘉王及面對口奏不預焉。

translations.literal: Before and after, together with attendants in joint memorials urging the emperor to visit the palace, there were thirty-five memorials in all; memorials submitted by the emperor himself numbered another sixteen chapters — not counting memorials to Chonghua, letters to Prince Ji, or oral submissions at face-to-face audiences.
translations.idiomatic: Before and after, he and his attendant colleagues submitted thirty-five joint memorials urging the emperor to visit the palace, and another sixteen memorials on his own — not counting memorials addressed to Chonghua Palace, letters to Prince Ji, or oral remonstrance at face-to-face audiences.

sentences.zh: 寧宗嗣位，人心始定。

translations.literal: When Ningzong succeeded to the throne, people's hearts were at last settled.
translations.idiomatic: When Ningzong succeeded to the throne, public sentiment at last settled.

sentences.zh: 拜點端明殿學士、簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: Dian was appointed Academician of the Hall for Illuminating Governance and Deputy Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Dian was appointed Academician of the Hall for Illuminating Governance and signing secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 上有事明堂，點扈從齋宮，得疾卒，年四十五。

translations.literal: The emperor was performing rites at the Bright Hall; Dian accompanied him to the fasting palace, fell ill, and died, aged forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor performed rites at the Bright Hall, Dian accompanied him to the fasting palace, fell ill, and died at forty-five.

sentences.zh: 贈太保，諡「文恭」。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded Grand Guardian and given the posthumous title "Wengong" (Cultured and Reverent).
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Guardian and given the posthumous title Wengong (Cultured and Reverent).

sentences.zh: 點天性孝友，無矯激崖異之行，而端介有守，義利之辨皎如。

translations.literal: Dian was by nature filial and fraternal; he had no affected, extreme, or eccentric conduct, yet was upright and principled, with the distinction between righteousness and profit as clear as daylight.
translations.idiomatic: By nature Dian was filial and fraternal; he had no affected or eccentric ways, yet he was upright and principled, with the distinction between righteousness and profit as clear as daylight.

sentences.zh: 或謂天下事非才不辦，點曰：「當先論其心，心苟不正，才雖過人，果何取哉！」

translations.literal: Some said that affairs under Heaven cannot be managed without talent. Dian said: "One should first judge the heart — if the heart is not upright, however surpassing one's talent, of what use is it?"
translations.idiomatic: Some said that affairs of state cannot be managed without talent. Dian said: "One must first judge the heart — if the heart is not upright, however great one's talent, what use is it?"

sentences.zh: 宰相趙汝愚嘗泣謂寧宗曰：「黃裳、羅點相繼淪謝，二臣不幸，天下之不幸也。」

translations.literal: Chief Minister Zhao Ruyu once wept and said to Ningzong: "Huang Chang and Luo Dian have in succession passed away — the misfortune of these two ministers is the misfortune of the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Zhao Ruyu once wept and told Ningzong: "Huang Chang and Luo Dian have died one after another — their loss is the realm's loss."

sentences.zh: 紹熙四年，守監察御史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shaoxi, he served as Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxi 4 (1193), he served as Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 蜀將吳挺死，度言：「挺子曦必納賂求襲位，若因而授之，恐為他日患，乞分其兵柄。」

translations.literal: When the Sichuan general Wu Ting died, Du said: "Ting's son Xi will surely pay bribes to seek to inherit his post; if he is granted it for that reason, I fear it will become trouble in days to come — I beg that his military authority be divided."
translations.idiomatic: When the Sichuan general Wu Ting died, Du said: "Ting's son Xi will surely pay bribes to seek to inherit his father's command; if the post is granted him, it may become trouble later — I beg that his military authority be divided."

sentences.zh: 宰相難之。

translations.literal: The chief minister found this difficult to accept.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister found this difficult to accept.

sentences.zh: 後曦割關外四州賂金人求王蜀，果如度言。

translations.literal: Later Xi ceded the four prefectures beyond the passes to the Jurchens as bribes to be made king of Shu — just as Du had said.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xi ceded the four prefectures beyond the passes to the Jurchens as bribes to be made king of Shu — just as Du had predicted.

sentences.zh: 光宗以疾不過重華宮，度上書切諫，連疏極陳父子相親之義，且言：「太白晝見犯天關，熒惑、勾芒行入太微，其占為亂兵入宮。」

translations.literal: Because Guangzong was ill and did not visit Chonghua Palace, Du submitted a memorial of urgent remonstrance; in successive memorials he fully set forth the meaning of close affection between father and son, and said: "The Great White star appeared in daylight and violated the Gate of Heaven; Mars and Gou Mang entered the Supreme Palace Enclosure — the omen is disorder and soldiers entering the palace."
translations.idiomatic: Because Guangzong was ill and did not visit Chonghua Palace, Du submitted urgent memorials of remonstrance; in successive submissions he fully set forth the bond between father and son, and said: "The Great White star appeared by day and violated the Gate of Heaven; Mars and Gou Mang entered the Supreme Palace Enclosure — the omen is disorder and armed men entering the palace."

sentences.zh: 以諫不聽，乞罷去。

translations.literal: Because his remonstrance went unheeded, he requested dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Because his remonstrance went unheeded, he requested dismissal.

sentences.zh: 又言：「以孝事君則忠。

translations.literal: He also said: "Serving the ruler with filial piety is loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Serving the ruler with filial piety is loyalty.

sentences.zh: 臣父年垂八十，菽水不親，動經歲月，事親如此，何以為事君之忠。」

translations.literal: Your servant's father is nearly eighty; I have not personally tended him with even simple meals for months at a time. If I serve my parent thus, how can I claim loyal service to the ruler?"
translations.idiomatic: My father is nearly eighty; I have not personally tended him with even simple meals for months at a time. If I serve my parent thus, how can I claim loyal service to the ruler?"

sentences.zh: 蓋託已為諭，冀因有以感悟上心。

translations.literal: This was in effect using himself as an analogy, hoping thereby to move the emperor's heart.
translations.idiomatic: This was in effect using himself as an analogy, hoping thereby to move the emperor's heart.

sentences.zh: 韓侂胄用事，丞相留正去國，侂胄知度嘗與正論事不合，欲諷使擠之。

translations.literal: When Han Tuozhou held power, Chief Minister Liu Zheng left the court. Tuozhou knew Du had often disagreed with Zheng on policy and wished to subtly induce others to squeeze Du out.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Tuozhou held power, Chief Minister Liu Zheng left the court. Tuozhou knew Du had often disagreed with Zheng on policy and wished to subtly induce others to force Du out.

sentences.zh: 度語同列曰：「丞相已去，擠之易耳，然長小人聲焰可乎？」

translations.literal: Du spoke to his colleagues, saying: "The chief minister is already gone; squeezing him out would be easy — yet is it permissible to extend the arrogance of petty men?"
translations.idiomatic: Du spoke to his colleagues, saying: "The chief minister is already gone; forcing him out would be easy — yet is it permissible to extend the arrogance of petty men?"

sentences.zh: 侂胄驟竊政柄，以意所好惡為威福。

translations.literal: Tuozhou abruptly seized governmental power and made reward and punishment according to his personal likes and dislikes.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou abruptly seized governmental power and made reward and punishment according to his personal likes and dislikes.

sentences.zh: 度具疏將論其姦，為侂胄所覺，御筆遽除度直顯謨閣、知平江府。

translations.literal: Du prepared a memorial to expose Tuozhou's treachery, but Tuozhou discovered it; by imperial brush he was suddenly appointed Direct Attendant at the Hall of Manifest Virtue and prefect of Pingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Du prepared a memorial to expose Tuozhou's treachery, but Tuozhou discovered it; by imperial brush he was suddenly appointed Direct Attendant at the Hall of Manifest Virtue and prefect of Pingjiang.

sentences.zh: 度言：「蔡京擅權，天下所由以亂。

translations.literal: Du said: "When Cai Jing monopolized power, the realm was thrown into disorder thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Du said: "When Cai Jing monopolized power, the realm was thrown into disorder thereby.

sentences.zh: 今侂胄假御筆逐臣，使俯首去，不得效一言，非為國之利也。」

translations.literal: Now Tuozhou uses the imperial brush to drive out your servant, making me bow my head and leave without being able to offer a single word — this is not to the state's advantage."
translations.idiomatic: Now Tuozhou uses the imperial brush to drive me out, making me bow my head and leave without being able to offer a single word — this is not to the state's advantage."

sentences.zh: 固辭。

translations.literal: He firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 丞相趙汝愚袖其疏入白，詔以沖佑祿歸養。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Zhao Ruyu tucked the memorial into his sleeve and reported it to the emperor; an edict granted him the salary of Chongyou and allowed him to return home to care for his parents.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Zhao Ruyu tucked the memorial into his sleeve and reported it to the emperor; an edict granted him the salary of Chongyou and allowed him to return home to care for his parents.

sentences.zh: 俄知婺州，坐不發覺縣令張元㢸贓罪，降罷。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed prefect of Wuzhou; he was demoted and dismissed for failing to detect the embezzlement of Magistrate Zhang Yuanbian.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed prefect of Wuzhou; he was demoted and dismissed for failing to detect the embezzlement of Magistrate Zhang Yuanbian.

sentences.zh: 自是紀綱一變，大權盡出侂胄，而黨論起矣。

translations.literal: From this time the standards of governance changed utterly; supreme power passed entirely to Tuozhou, and factional attacks began.
translations.idiomatic: From this time the standards of governance changed utterly; supreme power passed entirely to Tuozhou, and factional attacks began.

sentences.zh: 然侂胄素嚴憚度，不敢加害。

translations.literal: Yet Tuozhou had always deeply feared Du and dared not harm him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Tuozhou had always deeply feared Du and dared not harm him.

sentences.zh: 起知泉州，辭，乃進寶文閣，奉祠如故。

translations.literal: He was recalled to serve as prefect of Quanzhou; he declined, and was instead promoted to the Baowen Pavilion while continuing in a sinecure post as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as prefect of Quanzhou; he declined, and was instead promoted to the Baowen Pavilion while continuing in a sinecure post as before.

sentences.zh: 侂胄誅，天子思而召之，除太常少卿，尋兼國史院編修官、實錄院檢討官。

translations.literal: When Tuozhou was executed, the Son of Heaven thought of him and summoned him; he was appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and soon also Compiler at the National History Institute and Collator at the Veritable Records Institute.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuozhou was executed, the emperor thought of him and summoned him; he was appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and soon also Compiler at the National History Institute and Collator at the Veritable Records Institute.

sentences.zh: 朝論欲函侂胄首以泗州五千人還金，度以為辱國非之。

translations.literal: Court opinion wished to send Tuozhou's head in a box together with five thousand men from Sizhou back to the Jurchens; Du considered this humiliating to the state and objected.
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion wished to send Tuozhou's head in a box together with five thousand men from Sizhou back to the Jurchens; Du considered this humiliating to the state and objected.

sentences.zh: 權吏部侍郎兼修玉牒、同修國史、實錄院同修撰，屢移疾，以集英殿修撰知福州，遷寶謨閣待制。

translations.literal: He was Acting Vice Minister of Personnel while also revising the imperial genealogy, co-compiling the national history, and co-authoring the veritable records; he repeatedly cited illness and was appointed Compiler at the Hall of Assembled Excellence and prefect of Fuzhou, then promoted to Awaiting Commissioner at the Hall of Treasured Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Acting Vice Minister of Personnel while also revising the imperial genealogy, co-compiling the national history, and co-authoring the veritable records; he repeatedly cited illness and was appointed Compiler at the Hall of Assembled Excellence and prefect of Fuzhou, then promoted to Awaiting Commissioner at the Hall of Treasured Virtue.

sentences.zh: 始至，訟牒日千餘，度隨事裁決，日未中而畢。

translations.literal: When he first arrived, lawsuit documents exceeded a thousand per day; Du decided each according to its merits and finished before noon.
translations.idiomatic: When he first arrived, lawsuit documents exceeded a thousand per day; Du decided each on its merits and finished before noon.

sentences.zh: 進龍圖閣，知建康府兼江淮制置使，賜金帶以行。

translations.literal: He was promoted to the Hall of Dragon Designs, appointed prefect of Jiankang and Huai-Jiang Military Commissioner, and granted a golden belt for his journey.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to the Hall of Dragon Designs, appointed prefect of Jiankang and Huai-Jiang Military Commissioner, and granted a golden belt for his journey.

sentences.zh: 至金陵，罷科糴輸送之擾，活饑民百萬口，除見稅二十餘萬，擊降盜卞整，斬盜胡海首以獻，招歸業者九萬家。

translations.literal: When he reached Jinling, he abolished the harassment of forced grain purchases and transport, saving a million famine victims; he eliminated more than two hundred thousand in existing taxes; he attacked and forced the surrender of the bandit Bian Zheng and presented the severed head of the bandit Hu Hai; he brought back to their occupations ninety thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Jinling, he abolished the harassment of forced grain purchases and transport, saving a million famine victims; he eliminated more than two hundred thousand in existing taxes; he attacked and forced the surrender of the bandit Bian Zheng and presented the severed head of the bandit Hu Hai; he brought ninety thousand households back to their occupations.

sentences.zh: 侂胄嘗募雄淮軍，已收刺者十餘萬人，別屯數千人未有所屬，度憂其為患，人給錢四萬，復其役遣之。

translations.literal: Tuozhou had once recruited the Xionghuai Army; more than a hundred thousand who had already been registered were already assigned, but several thousand separately encamped had no affiliation; Du feared they would become a scourge, gave each man forty thousand cash, restored them to corvée exemption, and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou had once recruited the Xionghuai Army; more than a hundred thousand who had already been registered were already assigned, but several thousand separately encamped had no affiliation; Du feared they would become a scourge, gave each man forty thousand cash, restored them to corvée exemption, and sent them away.

sentences.zh: 遷寶謨閣直學士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Direct Academician at the Hall of Treasured Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Direct Academician at the Hall of Treasured Virtue.

sentences.zh: 度以人物為己任，推挽不休，每曰：「無以報國，惟有此耳。」

translations.literal: Du took recommending talent as his personal charge and pushed and pulled without cease; he often said: "I have no way to repay the state except this."
translations.idiomatic: Du took recommending talent as his personal charge and worked tirelessly at it; he often said: "I have no way to repay the state except this."

sentences.zh: 十上引年之請，不許，為禮部尚書兼侍讀。

translations.literal: Ten times he submitted requests to retire on grounds of age; he was not permitted, and was made Minister of Rites while also Lecturer-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Ten times he submitted requests to retire on grounds of age; he was not permitted, and was made Minister of Rites while also Lecturer-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 趣入覲，論藝祖垂萬世之統，一曰純用儒生，二曰務惜民力。

translations.literal: He was urgently summoned to audience and discussed the everlasting succession that Taizu bequeathed: first, to employ Confucian scholars exclusively; second, to cherish the people's strength.
translations.idiomatic: He was urgently summoned to audience and discussed the everlasting succession that Taizu bequeathed: first, to employ Confucian scholars exclusively; second, to cherish the people's strength.

sentences.zh: 上納其言。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his words.

sentences.zh: 謝病丐去，遂以煥章閣學士知隆興府。

translations.literal: He pleaded illness and begged to leave, and was then made Academician of the Huanzhang Pavilion and prefect of Longxing.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness and begged to leave, and was then made Academician of the Huanzhang Pavilion and prefect of Longxing.

sentences.zh: 歸越，提舉萬壽宮。

translations.literal: Returning to Yue, he was put in charge of the Wanshou Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to Yue, he was put in charge of the Wanshou Palace.

sentences.zh: 嘉定六年十月卒，進龍圖閣學士，贈通奉大夫。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the sixth year of Jiading, he died; he was posthumously promoted to Academician of the Hall of Dragon Designs and awarded the title of Palace Attendant for Offering.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Jiading 6 (1213), he died; he was posthumously promoted to Academician of the Hall of Dragon Designs and awarded the title of Palace Attendant for Offering.

sentences.zh: 度志在經世，而以學為本。

translations.literal: Du's aim was to order the age, yet he took learning as his foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Du's aim was to order the age, yet he took learning as his foundation.

sentences.zh: 作《詩》、《書》、《周禮》說。

translations.literal: He wrote commentaries on the Book of Poetry, Book of Documents, and Rites of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote commentaries on the Book of Poetry, Book of Documents, and Rites of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 著《史通》，抑僭竊，存大分，別為編年，不用前史法。

translations.literal: He composed Comprehensive Mirror of History, suppressing usurpers, preserving the great divisions, arranging events separately by year without using the methods of previous histories.
translations.idiomatic: He composed Comprehensive Mirror of History, suppressing usurpers, preserving the great divisions, arranging events separately by year without using the methods of previous histories.

sentences.zh: 至於天文、地理、井田、兵法，即近驗遠，可以據依，無迂陋牽合之病。

translations.literal: As for astronomy, geography, the well-field system, and military strategy, he verified the near to test the far — one could rely on his work without the sickness of forced or pedantic combination.
translations.idiomatic: As for astronomy, geography, the well-field system, and military strategy, he verified the near to test the far — one could rely on his work without the flaw of forced or pedantic combination.

sentences.zh: 又有《藝祖憲監》、《仁皇從諫錄》、《屯田便宜》、《歷代邊防》行於世。

translations.literal: He also had Administrator Taizu's Warning Mirror, Emperor Renzong's Record of Accepting Remonstrance, Expedient Measures for Colonization Fields, and Border Defense Through the Ages circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He also had Administrator Taizu's Warning Mirror, Emperor Renzong's Record of Accepting Remonstrance, Expedient Measures for Colonization Fields, and Border Defense Through the Ages circulating in the world.

sentences.zh: 婿周南。

translations.literal: His son-in-law was Zhou Nan.
translations.idiomatic: His son-in-law was Zhou Nan.

sentences.zh: 周南

translations.literal: Zhou Nan
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Nan

translations.literal: (Attached supplement)
translations.idiomatic: (Attached supplement)

sentences.zh: 周南，字南仲，平江人。

translations.literal: Zhou Nan, courtesy name Nanzhong, was a native of Pingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Nan, styled Nanzhong, came from Pingjiang.

sentences.zh: 年十六，遊學吳下，視時人業科舉，心陋之。

translations.literal: At sixteen he traveled to study in Wu, and looked on those of the time pursuing the examination career with contempt in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen he traveled to study in Wu, and looked with contempt on those of the day who pursued the examination career.

sentences.zh: 從葉適講學，頓悟捷得。

translations.literal: He studied under Ye Shi and gained sudden penetrating understanding with rapid progress.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Ye Shi and gained sudden penetrating understanding with rapid progress.

sentences.zh: 為文詞，雅麗精切，而皆達于時用，每以世道興廢為己任。

translations.literal: In composing literary pieces, his style was elegant, refined, and precise, yet all reached practical use; he always took the rise and fall of the age as his personal responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: In composing literary pieces, his style was elegant, refined, and precise, yet all served practical ends; he always took the rise and fall of the age as his personal responsibility.

sentences.zh: 登紹熙元年進士第，為池州教授。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the first year of Shaoxi and was appointed professor at Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He placed on the jinshi roll in Shaoxi 1 (1190) and was appointed professor at Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 會度以言忤當路，御史劾度，並南罷之。

translations.literal: When Du offended those in power with his words, the censor impeached Du and dismissed Nan along with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Du offended those in power with his words, the censor impeached Du and dismissed Nan along with him.

sentences.zh: 度與南俱入偽學黨。

translations.literal: Du and Nan both were placed in the False Learning faction.
translations.idiomatic: Du and Nan both were placed in the False Learning faction.

sentences.zh: 開禧三年，召試館職。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaixi, he was summoned for a qualifying examination for a palace post.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaixi 3 (1207), he was summoned for a qualifying examination for a palace post.

sentences.zh: 南對策詆權要，言者劾南，罷之，卒於家。

translations.literal: In the examination Nan's answers denounced the powerful; remonstrators impeached Nan and dismissed him; he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: In the examination Nan's answers denounced the powerful; remonstrators impeached Nan and dismissed him; he died at home.

sentences.zh: 南端行拱立，尺寸有程準。

translations.literal: Nan's bearing in walking and standing was measured; every inch had its standard.
translations.idiomatic: Nan's bearing in walking and standing was measured; every inch had its standard.

sentences.zh: 自賜第授文林郎，終身不進官，兩為館職，數月止。

translations.literal: From receiving the jinshi rank and appointment as Gentleman for Annotating Texts, he never advanced in office through his entire life; he held palace posts twice, each time for only a few months.
translations.idiomatic: From receiving the jinshi rank and appointment as Gentleman for Annotating Texts, he never advanced in office through his entire life; he held palace posts twice, each time for only a few months.

sentences.zh: 既絕意當世，弊衣惡食，挾書忘晝夜，曰：「此所以遺吾老，俟吾死也。」

translations.literal: Having utterly abandoned ambition for the age, he wore worn clothes and ate coarse food, carrying books day and night without rest, saying: "This is what I leave for my old age — I await my death with it."
translations.idiomatic: Having utterly abandoned ambition for public life, he wore worn clothes and ate coarse food, carrying books day and night without rest, saying: "This is what I leave for my old age — I await my death with it."

sentences.zh: 林大中

translations.literal: Lin Dazhong
translations.idiomatic: Lin Dazhong

sentences.zh: 林大中，字和叔，婺州永康人。

translations.literal: Lin Dazhong, courtesy name Heshu, was a native of Yongkang in Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Dazhong, styled Heshu, came from Yongkang in Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 入太學，登紹興三十年進士第，知撫州金谿縣。

translations.literal: He entered the Imperial University, passed the jinshi examination in the thirtieth year of Shaoxing, and served as magistrate of Jinxi County in Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Imperial University, placed on the jinshi roll in Shaoxing 30 (1160), and served as magistrate of Jinxi County in Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 郡督輸賦急，大中請寬其期，不聽，納告敕投劾而歸。

translations.literal: The prefecture supervisor pressed urgently for tax delivery; Dazhong requested extension of the deadline but was not heard; he submitted his commission of appointment and impeached himself, then returned home.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture supervisor pressed urgently for tax delivery; Dazhong requested extension of the deadline but was not heard; he submitted his commission of appointment and impeached himself, then returned home.

sentences.zh: 已而主太常寺簿。

translations.literal: Afterward he served as clerk of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he served as clerk of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 光宗受禪，除監察御史。

translations.literal: When Guangzong received the abdication, he was appointed Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangzong received the abdication, he was appointed Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 大中謂：「國之大事在祀，沿襲不正，非所以嚴典禮，妥神明。」

translations.literal: Dazhong said: "The great affairs of the state lie in sacrifice; when we continue inherited errors, we do not properly honor canonical rites and placate the spirits."
translations.idiomatic: Dazhong said: "The great affairs of the state lie in sacrifice; when we continue inherited errors, we do not properly honor canonical rites and placate the spirits."

sentences.zh: 上疏言：「臣昨簿正奉常，實陪廟祀，見其祝於神者，或舛于文；

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant yesterday, as clerk rectifying matters at the Court of Grand Harmony, actually accompanied the temple sacrifices, and saw that in addressing the spirits in prayer, some texts were at odds with the proper wording;
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial saying: "Yesterday, as clerk rectifying matters at the Court of Grand Harmony, I actually accompanied the temple sacrifices, and saw that in addressing the spirits in prayer, some texts were at odds with the proper wording;

sentences.zh: 稱於神者，或訛其字；

translations.literal: in naming the spirits, some characters were wrong;
translations.idiomatic: in naming the spirits, some characters were wrong;

sentences.zh: 所宜厚者，或簡不虔；

translations.literal: what should be ample was sometimes treated with careless lack of reverence;
translations.idiomatic: what should be ample was sometimes treated with careless lack of reverence;

sentences.zh: 所宜先者，或廢不用；

translations.literal: what should come first was sometimes discarded and not used;
translations.idiomatic: what should come first was sometimes discarded and not used;

sentences.zh: 更制器服，或歲月太疏；

translations.literal: when changing vessels and vestments, the interval between years was sometimes too long;
translations.idiomatic: when changing vessels and vestments, the interval between years was sometimes too long;

sentences.zh: 夙興行事，或時刻太早：是皆禮意所未順，人情所未安也。」

translations.literal: when rising early to perform the rites, the hour was sometimes too early — all these were where ritual meaning had not yet been aligned and human sentiment had not yet been settled."
translations.idiomatic: when rising early to perform the rites, the hour was sometimes too early — all these were where ritual meaning had not yet been aligned and human sentiment had not yet been settled."

sentences.zh: 一日，御劄示大中，謂言事覺察，宜遵舊例。

translations.literal: One day the emperor's personal note was shown to Dazhong, saying that remonstrance should be observed according to old precedent.
translations.idiomatic: One day the emperor's personal note was shown to Dazhong, saying that remonstrance should be observed according to old precedent.

sentences.zh: 大中曰：「臺臣不當逾分守，固如聖訓，然必抗直敢言，乃為稱職。」

translations.literal: Dazhong said: "Censorial officials ought not exceed their proper bounds — that is indeed as Your Majesty instructs; yet only by being upright and daring to speak can one fulfill the post."
translations.idiomatic: Dazhong said: "Censorial officials ought not exceed their proper bounds — that is indeed as Your Majesty instructs; yet only by being upright and daring to speak can one fulfill the post."

sentences.zh: 遷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Palace Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Palace Censor.

sentences.zh: 奏言：「進退人才，當觀其趣向之大體，不當責其行事之小節。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "In promoting and demoting talent, one should observe the general direction of their aims, and should not hold them accountable for small details of conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "In promoting and demoting talent, one should observe the general direction of their aims, and should not hold them accountable for small details of conduct.

sentences.zh: 趣向果正，雖小節可責，不失為君子；

translations.literal: If their direction is indeed upright, even if small details are blameworthy, they remain gentlemen;
translations.idiomatic: If their direction is indeed upright, even if small details are blameworthy, they remain gentlemen;

sentences.zh: 趣向不正，雖小節可喜，不失為小人。」

translations.literal: If the direction is not upright, even if small details are pleasing, they remain petty men."
translations.idiomatic: If the direction is not upright, even if small details are pleasing, they remain petty men."

sentences.zh: 又論：「今日之事，莫大于仇恥未復。

translations.literal: He also argued: "Of affairs today, none is greater than that the humiliation has not yet been avenged.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued: "Of affairs today, none is greater than that the humiliation has not yet been avenged.

sentences.zh: 此事未就，則此念不可忘。

translations.literal: Until this matter is accomplished, this resolve must not be forgotten.
translations.idiomatic: Until this matter is accomplished, this resolve must not be forgotten.

sentences.zh: 此念存于心，於以來天下之才，作天下之氣，倡天下之義。

translations.literal: With this resolve kept in the heart, by it one gathers talent under Heaven, rouses the spirit under Heaven, and champions righteousness under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: With this resolve kept in the heart, by it one gathers talent under Heaven, rouses the spirit under Heaven, and champions righteousness under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 此義既明，則事之條目可得而言，治功可得而成矣。」

translations.literal: Once this principle is clear, the items of policy can be spoken of, and governing achievement can be achieved."
translations.idiomatic: Once this principle is clear, the items of policy can be spoken of, and governing achievement can be achieved.

sentences.zh: 陳賈以靜江守臣入奏，大中極論其「庸回亡識，嘗表裏王淮，創為道學之目，陰廢正人。

translations.literal: When Chen Jia came to court to report as military governor of Jingjiang, Dazhong argued vehemently against him: "Mediocre, obsequious, and devoid of judgment; he once acted inside and outside with Wang Huai, created the category of Learning of the Way, and covertly displaced upright men.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Jia came to court as military governor of Jingjiang, Dazhong spoke forcefully against him: "He is mediocre, fawning, and without judgment; he once worked hand in glove with Wang Huai, invented the label of Learning of the Way, and secretly removed worthy men from office.

sentences.zh: 儻許入奏，必再留中，善類聞之，紛然引去，非所以靖國。」

translations.literal: If he is permitted to enter and report, the memorial will surely again be kept within; when good men hear of it, they will one after another withdraw — this is not the way to settle the state."
translations.idiomatic: If he is allowed to report at court, the memorial will surely be held back again; when worthy officials hear of it, they will withdraw one after another — this is no way to bring stability to the realm.

sentences.zh: 命遂寢。

translations.literal: The order was then dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The order was then dropped.

sentences.zh: 紹熙二年春，雷電交作，有旨訪時政闕失。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year of Shaoxi, thunder and lightning occurred together; an edict was issued to inquire into omissions and failures in current policy.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year of Shaoxi, thunder and lightning struck together, and an edict was issued asking officials to report omissions and failures in current policy.

sentences.zh: 大中以事多中出，乃上疏曰：「仲春雷電，大雪繼作，以類求之，則陰勝陽之明驗也。

translations.literal: Because many affairs were issued from within the palace, Dazhong submitted a memorial saying: "In mid-spring, thunder and lightning; heavy snow followed — seeking parallels by category, this is clear proof of yin overcoming yang.
translations.idiomatic: Because many matters were being decided inside the palace, Dazhong submitted a memorial saying: "In mid-spring came thunder and lightning, followed by heavy snow — if we read these signs by category, they are clear proof that yin is overpowering yang.

sentences.zh: 蓋男為陽，而女為陰，君子為陽，而小人為陰。

translations.literal: For man is yang and woman is yin; the gentleman is yang and the petty man is yin.
translations.idiomatic: Man is yang and woman is yin; the gentleman is yang and the petty man is yin.

sentences.zh: 當辨邪正，毋使小人得以間君子。

translations.literal: One must distinguish heterodox from orthodox, and must not let petty men be able to come between gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: We must distinguish the heterodox from the orthodox and must not let petty men drive a wedge between gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 當思正始之道，毋使女謁之得行。」

translations.literal: One must reflect on the Way of the Correct Beginning, and must not let women who gain access to power have their way."
translations.idiomatic: We must keep in mind the Way of the Correct Beginning and must not let palace women who gain influence have their way."

sentences.zh: 司諫鄧馹以言事移將作監，大中言：「臺諫以論事不合而遷，臣恐天下以陛下為不能容。」

translations.literal: Supervising Remonstrance Officer Deng Ji was transferred to Director of Palace Construction for his policy remonstrances; Dazhong said: "When censorial remonstrance officials are transferred because their policy views did not accord, I fear all under Heaven will take Your Majesty to be incapable of tolerance."
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Remonstrance Officer Deng Ji was transferred to Director of Palace Construction after speaking on policy matters; Dazhong said: "When remonstrance officials are moved because their views on policy do not accord with the court, I fear the realm will conclude that Your Majesty cannot tolerate dissent.

sentences.zh: 守侍御史兼侍講。

translations.literal: He retained the post of Supervising Secretariat Censor and additionally served as Lecturer-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He retained his post as Supervising Secretariat Censor and was also made Lecturer-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 知潭州趙善俊得旨奏事，大中上疏劾善俊，而言宗室汝愚之賢當召。

translations.literal: Zhao ShanJun, prefect of Tanzhou, received permission to report at court; Dazhong submitted a memorial impeaching ShanJun and saying that the worthy imperial clansman Ruyu ought to be summoned.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao ShanJun, prefect of Tanzhou, received permission to report at court, Dazhong submitted a memorial impeaching ShanJun and urging that the worthy imperial clansman Zhao Ruyu ought to be recalled.

sentences.zh: 上用其言，召汝愚而出善俊與郡。

translations.literal: The emperor adopted his words, summoned Ruyu, and sent ShanJun out to a prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed his advice, recalled Ruyu, and sent ShanJun out to serve in a prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時江、淮、荊、襄為國巨屏，而權任頗輕。

translations.literal: At that time the Jiang, Huai, Jing, and Xiang regions formed the state's great bulwark, yet authority and responsibility were rather slight.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Jiang, Huai, Jing, and Xiang regions formed the realm's great defensive screen, yet the authority vested in their commanders was rather slight.

sentences.zh: 大中言：「宜選行實材略之人，付以江、淮、荊、襄經理之任。

translations.literal: Dazhong said: "One should select men of proven conduct and strategic talent and entrust them with responsibility for administering the Jiang, Huai, Jing, and Xiang regions.
translations.idiomatic: Dazhong said: "We should select men of proven character and strategic ability and entrust them with responsibility for governing the Jiang, Huai, Jing, and Xiang regions.

sentences.zh: 舊制河北、陝西分為四路，以文臣為大帥，武臣副之。

translations.literal: Under the old system, Hebei and Shaanxi were divided into four circuits; civil officials served as chief commanders and military officials as their deputies.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system, Hebei and Shaanxi were divided into four circuits, with civil officials as chief commanders and military officials as their deputies.

sentences.zh: 中興初，沿江置制置使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Restoration, commissioners for military affairs were established along the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Restoration, military affairs commissioners were established along the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 自秦檜罷三大將兵權，專歸武臣，而江東、荊、襄帥臣不復領制置之職。

translations.literal: Since Qin Hui stripped the three great generals of military authority and concentrated it solely in military officials, the commanders of Jiangdong, Jing, and Xiang no longer held the post of commissioner for military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Qin Hui stripped the three great generals of their military authority and returned command solely to military officials, the commanders of Jiangdong, Jing, and Xiang no longer held the post of military affairs commissioner.

sentences.zh: 宜仍舊制置，而以諸將為副，久其任，重其權，則邊防立而國勢張矣。」

translations.literal: One should restore the old system of commissioners for military affairs, with the various generals as deputies; extend their tenures and increase their authority — then frontier defense will be established and the state's strength will be asserted."
translations.idiomatic: We should restore the old system of military affairs commissioners, with the various generals as deputies; if we extend their terms and increase their authority, the frontier will be secured and the realm's strength will be restored."

sentences.zh: 江、浙四路民苦折帛和買重輸，大中曰：「有產則有稅，於稅絹而科折帛，猶可言也，如和買折帛則重為民害。

translations.literal: The people of the four circuits in Jiang and Zhe suffered from the heavy burdens of zhebo silk payments and government cloth purchase; Dazhong said: "Those with property pay taxes — to assess zhebo on the basis of tax silk can still be explained; but zhebo on government purchase cloth is a heavy harm to the people.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the four circuits in Jiang and Zhe suffered under the heavy burdens of zhebo silk payments and government cloth purchases; Dazhong said: "Those with property pay taxes — to assess zhebo on the basis of tax silk can still be defended; but zhebo levied on government purchase cloth is a grave injury to the people.

sentences.zh: 蓋自咸平馬元方建言于春預支本錢濟其乏絕，至夏秋使之輸納，則是先支錢而後輸絹。

translations.literal: For since the Xianping era, Ma Yuanfang proposed advancing principal funds in spring to relieve their shortage, then having them deliver payment by summer and autumn — this was first advancing money and then requiring silk.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Xianping era, when Ma Yuanfang proposed advancing principal funds in spring to relieve shortages and having the people deliver payment by summer and autumn, the practice was to pay out money first and only then receive silk in return.

sentences.zh: 其後則錢鹽分給，又其後則直取於民，今又令納折帛錢，以兩縑折一縑之直，大失立法初意。」
