translations.literal: Later money and salt were distributed separately; later still it was taken directly from the people; now they are again required to pay zhebo in cash, reckoning the price of one bolt of silk at the cost of two — greatly departing from the original intent of the law."
translations.idiomatic: Later money and salt were distributed separately; still later payments were taken directly from the people; and now they are required to pay zhebo in cash, reckoning one bolt of silk at the price of two — a gross departure from the law's original intent.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以其言為減所輸者三歲。

translations.literal: The court, on the strength of his words, reduced what was owed for three years.
translations.idiomatic: On the strength of his argument, the court reduced the amount owed for three years.

sentences.zh: 馬大同為戶部，大中劾其用法峻。

translations.literal: Ma Datong served as Minister of Revenue; Dazhong impeached him for harsh application of the law.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Datong was serving as Minister of Revenue when Dazhong impeached him for applying the law with excessive severity.

sentences.zh: 上欲易置他部，大中曰：「是嘗為刑部，固以深刻稱。」

translations.literal: The emperor wished to transfer him to another ministry; Dazhong said: "He once served in the Ministry of Punishments and was indeed known for severity."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to transfer him to another ministry; Dazhong said: "He once served in the Ministry of Punishments and was already known for harshness.

sentences.zh: 章三上不報。

translations.literal: His memorials were submitted three times without response.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted memorials three times without receiving a response.

sentences.zh: 又論大理少卿宋之瑞，章四上，又不報。

translations.literal: He again criticized Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review Song Zhirui; four memorials were submitted, again without response.
translations.idiomatic: He also criticized Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review Song Zhirui; he submitted four memorials, again without response.

sentences.zh: 大中以言不行，求去，改吏部侍郎，辭不拜，乃除大中直寶謨閣，而大同、之瑞俱與郡。

translations.literal: Because his words went unheeded, Dazhong asked to leave; he was transferred to Vice Minister of Civil Personnel but declined to accept the appointment; he was then granted direct appointment to the Baomo Pavilion, while Datong and Zhirui were both sent to prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When his advice went unheeded, Dazhong asked to leave office; he was transferred to Vice Minister of Civil Personnel but declined the appointment; he was then made a direct attendant of the Baomo Pavilion, while Datong and Zhirui were both sent out to prefectures.

sentences.zh: 初，占星者謂朱熹曰：「某星示變，正人當之，其在林和叔耶？」

translations.literal: Earlier, an astrologer told Zhu Xi: "A certain star shows change; a worthy man will meet it — could it be Lin Heshu?"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, an astrologer told Zhu Xi: "A certain star shows a portent of change; a worthy man will bear it — could it be Lin Heshu?

sentences.zh: 至是，熹貽書朝士曰：「聞林和叔入臺，無一事不中的，去國一節，風義凜然，當于古人中求之。」

translations.literal: At this time, Xi wrote to court officials: "I hear that since Lin Heshu entered the censorate, not a single thing he has done has missed its mark; in one act of leaving the capital, his integrity was imposing — one should seek his like among the ancients."
translations.idiomatic: At this point Xi wrote to court officials: "I hear that since Lin Heshu entered the censorate, not one of his actions has missed its mark; in a single act of leaving the capital, his moral bearing was imposing — one must seek his like among the ancients.

sentences.zh: 給事中尤袤、中書舍人樓鑰上疏云：「大中言官，當與被論者有別。」

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary You Mao and Secretariat Drafter Luo Key submitted memorials saying: "As a remonstrance official, Dazhong ought to be distinguished from those he has criticized."
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary You Mao and Secretariat Drafter Luo Key submitted memorials saying: "As a remonstrance official, Dazhong ought to be treated differently from those he has criticized.

sentences.zh: 尋命知寧國府，又移贛州。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to serve as prefect of Ningguo Prefecture, and was later transferred to Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed prefect of Ningguo Prefecture, and was later transferred to Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 寧宗即位，召還，試中書舍人，遷給事中，尋兼侍講。

translations.literal: When Ningzong ascended the throne, Dazhong was recalled; he passed examination for Secretariat Drafter, was promoted to Supervising Secretary, and soon additionally served as Lecturer-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: When Ningzong ascended the throne, Dazhong was recalled; he passed examination for Secretariat Drafter, was promoted to Supervising Secretary, and soon also served as Lecturer-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 知閤門事韓侂胄來謁，大中接之無他語，陰請內交，大中笑而卻之，侂胄怨由此始。

translations.literal: Han Tuozhou, Director of the Palace Gate, came to pay a visit; Dazhong received him with no other words; Tuozhou secretly sought an inside connection, and Dazhong laughed and refused him — Tuozhou's resentment began from this.
translations.idiomatic: Han Tuozhou, Director of the Palace Gate, came to call on him; Dazhong received him without another word; Tuozhou secretly sought a private alliance, and Dazhong laughed and refused him — Tuozhou's resentment began from that moment.

sentences.zh: 會吏部侍郎彭龜年抗論侂胄，侂胄轉一官與內祠，龜年除煥章閣待制與郡。

translations.literal: When Vice Minister of Civil Personnel Peng Guinian sternly argued against Tuozhou, Tuozhou was granted one rank promotion and an inner temple post; Guinian was appointed Attendant Gentleman of the Huanzhang Pavilion and sent to a prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Vice Minister of Civil Personnel Peng Guinian spoke out forcefully against Tuozhou, Tuozhou was promoted one rank and given an inner temple post; Guinian was appointed Attendant Gentleman of the Huanzhang Pavilion and sent out to a prefecture.

sentences.zh: 大中同中書舍人樓鑰繳奏曰：「陛下眷禮僚舊，一旦龍飛，延問無虛日。

translations.literal: Dazhong together with Secretariat Drafter Luo Key submitted a sealed memorial of remonstrance saying: "Your Majesty has cherished and honored old associates; once the dragon flew, you extended inquiries without a vacant day.
translations.idiomatic: Dazhong and Secretariat Drafter Luo Key submitted a sealed remonstrance saying: "Your Majesty has cherished and honored your old associates; once you ascended the throne, you sought their counsel day after day.

sentences.zh: 不三數月間，或死或斥，賴龜年一人尚留，今又去之，四方謂其以盡言得罪，恐傷政體。

translations.literal: Within barely three months, some died and some were dismissed; only Guinian alone remained — now he too is removed; the four quarters say he was punished for speaking fully — I fear this will harm the body of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Within scarcely three months, some had died and others had been dismissed; only Guinian remained — and now he too is being removed; the four quarters will say he was punished for speaking his mind fully, and I fear this will damage the integrity of governance.

sentences.zh: 且一去一留，恩意不侔。

translations.literal: Moreover, one dismissed and one retained — the grace shown is not equal.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, one man is dismissed and another retained — the favor shown them is not equal.

sentences.zh: 去者日遠，不復侍左右。

translations.literal: The dismissed man grows daily more distant and no longer attends at your side.
translations.idiomatic: The dismissed man grows daily more distant and can no longer attend at your side.

sentences.zh: 留者內祠，則召見無時。

translations.literal: The one retained has an inner temple post, so audiences may be summoned at any time.
translations.idiomatic: The one retained holds an inner temple post and may be summoned for audience at any time.

sentences.zh: 請留龜年經筵，而命侂胄以外任，則事體適平，人無可言者。」

translations.literal: We ask that Guinian be kept at the classic exposition, and that Tuozhou be ordered to an outside appointment — then the matter will be properly balanced, and people will have nothing to say."
translations.idiomatic: We ask that Guinian be kept at the classic exposition and that Tuozhou be assigned to an outside post — then the matter will be properly balanced and no one will have grounds for complaint.

sentences.zh: 有旨：「龜年已為優異，侂胄本無過尤，可並書行。」

translations.literal: An edict came: "Guinian has already been treated with exceptional favor; Tuozhou originally had no fault — let both appointments proceed as written."
translations.idiomatic: An edict came: "Guinian has already been treated with exceptional favor; Tuozhou originally had no fault — let both appointments proceed as written.

sentences.zh: 大中復同奏：「龜年除職與郡以為優異，則侂胄之轉承宣使非優異乎？

translations.literal: Dazhong again memorialized jointly: "If Guinian's appointment to office and prefecture is taken as exceptional favor, is not Tuozhou's promotion to Commissioner for Graceful Decrees also exceptional favor?
translations.idiomatic: Dazhong again submitted a joint memorial: "If Guinian's appointment to office and prefecture counts as exceptional favor, does not Tuozhou's promotion to Commissioner for Graceful Decrees count as exceptional favor as well?

sentences.zh: 若謂侂胄本無過尤，則龜年論事實出於愛君之忱，豈得為過？

translations.literal: If Tuozhou originally had no fault, then Guinian's policy arguments truly arose from devotion to the ruler — how can that count as fault?
translations.idiomatic: If Tuozhou originally had no fault, then Guinian's policy arguments truly arose from devotion to the ruler — how can that be counted as fault?

sentences.zh: 龜年既以決去，侂胄難於獨留，宜畀外任或外祠，以慰公議。」

translations.literal: Since Guinian has already resolved to leave, it is difficult for Tuozhou alone to remain; he should be given an outside appointment or outside temple post, to satisfy public opinion."
translations.idiomatic: Since Guinian has already resolved to leave, it is difficult for Tuozhou alone to remain; he should be given an outside appointment or an outside temple post to satisfy public opinion.

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: They were not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: They were not heeded.

sentences.zh: 太府寺丞呂祖儉以上書攻侂胄，謫置韶州，大中捄之。

translations.literal: Supervising Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury Lü Zujian attacked Tuozhou in a memorial; he was demoted and banished to Shaozhou; Dazhong rescued him.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury Lü Zujian attacked Tuozhou in a memorial and was demoted and banished to Shaozhou; Dazhong intervened on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 汪義端頃為御史，以論趙汝愚去，至是侂胄引為右史，大中駁之。

translations.literal: Wang Yiduan had recently been a censor and was dismissed for criticizing Zhao Ruyu; at this time Tuozhou brought him in as Right Drafter; Dazhong opposed it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yiduan had recently served as a censor and was dismissed for criticizing Zhao Ruyu; now Tuozhou brought him back as Right Drafter, and Dazhong opposed the appointment.

sentences.zh: 改吏部侍郎，不拜，以煥章閣待制知慶元府。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Civil Personnel but declined the appointment; as Attendant Gentleman of the Huanzhang Pavilion he was made prefect of Qingyuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Civil Personnel but declined to accept the appointment; as Attendant Gentleman of the Huanzhang Pavilion he was appointed prefect of Qingyuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 城南民田，潮溢不可種，大中捐公帑治石築之，民不知役而蒙其利。

translations.literal: South of the city, people's fields were flooded by tides and could not be planted; Dazhong drew from public funds to have stone dikes built; the people knew no corvée labor yet received the benefit.
translations.idiomatic: South of the city, people's fields were flooded by tides and could not be planted; Dazhong drew on public funds to have stone dikes built; the people performed no corvée labor yet reaped the benefit.

sentences.zh: 郡訛言夜有妖，大中謂此必黠賊所為，立捕黥之，人情遂安。

translations.literal: The prefecture had a false report that demons appeared by night; Dazhong said this must be the work of cunning thieves; he immediately had them captured and tattooed as punishment, and public sentiment was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: A false rumor spread through the prefecture that demons appeared by night; Dazhong said this must be the work of cunning thieves; he had them captured at once and tattooed as punishment, and public sentiment was restored.

sentences.zh: 丐祠，得請。

translations.literal: He requested a temple post and was granted it.
translations.idiomatic: He requested a temple post and was granted it.

sentences.zh: 給事中許及之繳駁，遂削職。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Xu Jizhi submitted a sealed remonstrance rejecting it, and his rank was then reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Xu Jizhi submitted a sealed remonstrance rejecting the appointment, and Dazhong's rank was then reduced.

sentences.zh: 後提舉沖佑觀。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed director of the Chongyou Observatory.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed director of the Chongyou Observatory.

sentences.zh: 乞休致，復元職。

translations.literal: He requested retirement and had his original rank restored.
translations.idiomatic: He requested retirement and had his original rank restored.

sentences.zh: 監宗御史林采論列，再落職，尋復之。

translations.literal: Supervisory Censor of the Imperial Clan Lin Cai listed charges against him; his rank was reduced again, but soon restored.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisory Censor of the Imperial Clan Lin Cai listed charges against him; his rank was reduced again, but was soon restored.

sentences.zh: 大中罷歸，屏居十二年，未嘗以得喪關其心，作園龜潭之上，客至，擷杞菊，取溪魚，觴酒賦詩，時事一不以掛口。

translations.literal: After Dazhong was dismissed and returned home, he lived in seclusion for twelve years; he never let gain or loss touch his heart; he made a garden above Guitan; when guests came, he would pick wolfberry and chrysanthemum, take fish from the stream, raise cups and compose poems — current affairs he never once brought to his lips.
translations.idiomatic: After Dazhong was dismissed and returned home, he lived in seclusion for twelve years; gain and loss never touched his heart; he made a garden above Guitan, and when guests came he would pick wolfberry and chrysanthemum, take fish from the stream, raise cups and compose poems — never once speaking of current affairs.

sentences.zh: 客或勸大中通侂胄書，大中曰：「吾為夕郎時，一言承意，豈閒居至今日耶？」

translations.literal: When guests sometimes urged Dazhong to send letters to Tuozhou, Dazhong said: "When I was Evening Gentleman, one word that pleased him — and I would be a reclusive dweller even to this day?"
translations.idiomatic: When guests sometimes urged Dazhong to send letters to Tuozhou, Dazhong said: "When I was Evening Gentleman, had I spoken one word to please him, would I be living in seclusion even to this day?

sentences.zh: 客曰：「縱不求福，盍亦免禍。」

translations.literal: The guest said: "Even if you do not seek good fortune, should you not at least avoid calamity?"
translations.idiomatic: The guest said: "Even if you do not seek good fortune, should you not at least try to avoid calamity?

sentences.zh: 大中曰：「福不可求而得，禍可懼而免耶？」

translations.literal: Dazhong said: "Good fortune cannot be sought and obtained — can calamity be feared and avoided?"
translations.idiomatic: Dazhong said: "Good fortune cannot be sought and obtained — can calamity be feared away and avoided?

sentences.zh: 侂胄既召兵畔，大中謂：「今日欲安民，非息兵不可；

translations.literal: When Tuozhou had already mobilized the armies and rebellion spread, Dazhong said: "Today, if one wishes to settle the people, one cannot do so without ceasing hostilities;
translations.idiomatic: When Tuozhou had mobilized the armies and the frontier fell into turmoil, Dazhong said: "Today, if we wish to settle the people, we cannot do so without ceasing hostilities;

sentences.zh: 欲息兵，非去侂胄不可。」

translations.literal: To cease hostilities, removing Tuozhou is indispensable."
translations.idiomatic: To cease hostilities, removing Tuozhou is indispensable."

sentences.zh: 及侂胄誅，即召見，落致仕，試吏部尚書，言：「呂祖儉以言侂胄得罪，死於瘴鄉，雖贈官畀職，而公議未厭。

translations.literal: When Tuozhou was executed, Dazhong was immediately summoned for audience; his retirement was revoked and he was appointed acting Minister of Civil Personnel; he said: "Lü Zujian was punished for speaking against Tuozhou and died in the miasma-ridden south; although offices and titles were posthumously granted, public opinion is still unsatisfied.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuozhou was executed, Dazhong was immediately summoned for audience; his retirement was revoked and he was appointed acting Minister of Civil Personnel; he said: "Lü Zujian was punished for speaking against Tuozhou and died in the miasma-ridden south; although offices and titles were posthumously granted, public opinion is still unsatisfied.

sentences.zh: 彭龜年面奏侂胄過尤，朱熹論侂胄竊弄威柄，皆為中傷，降官鐫職，卒以老死，宜優加旌表。

translations.literal: Peng Guinian personally memorialized Tuozhou's faults; Zhu Xi argued that Tuozhou usurped and wielded power — both were slandered, demoted, and had their ranks carved away, and ended by dying in old age; they should be specially honored and publicly commended.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Guinian personally memorialized Tuozhou's faults; Zhu Xi argued that Tuozhou usurped and wielded power — both were slandered, demoted, and stripped of rank, and ended by dying in old age; they should be specially honored and publicly commended.

sentences.zh: 其他因譏切侂胄以得罪者，望量其輕重而旌別之，以伸被罪者之冤。」

translations.literal: As for others who were punished for sharply criticizing Tuozhou, I hope Your Majesty will weigh degrees of severity and distinguish honors accordingly, to vindicate those who were wronged."
translations.idiomatic: As for others who were punished for sharply criticizing Tuozhou, I hope Your Majesty will weigh the severity of each case and distinguish honors accordingly, to vindicate those who were wronged.

sentences.zh: 除端明殿學士、簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Academician of the Duanming Hall and Assistant Commissioner of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Academician of the Duanming Hall and Assistant Commissioner of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 嘉定改元，兼太子賓客。

translations.literal: When the era was changed to Jiading, he additionally served as Guest of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the era was changed to Jiading, he additionally served as Guest of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 嘗議講和事，上曰：「朕不憚屈己為民，講和之後，亦欲與卿等革侂胄弊政作家活耳。」

translations.literal: Once when peace negotiations were discussed, the emperor said: "I do not shrink from humbling myself for the people; after peace is concluded, I also wish to work with you all to reform Tuozhou's corrupt policies and make a living home for the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Once when peace negotiations were discussed, the emperor said: "I do not shrink from humbling myself for the people; after peace is concluded, I also wish to work with you to reform Tuozhou's corrupt policies and rebuild the realm.

sentences.zh: 大中頓首曰：「陛下言及此，宗社生靈之福也。」

translations.literal: Dazhong bowed his head and said: "That Your Majesty speaks of this is the fortune of the altars of state and the living people."
translations.idiomatic: Dazhong bowed his head and said: "That Your Majesty speaks of this is a blessing for the altars of state and for the people.

sentences.zh: 每語所親云：「吾年垂八十，豈堪勞勩，徒以和議未成，思體承聖訓，以革弊幸為經久之計。

translations.literal: He often told those close to him: "I am approaching eighty — how could I bear strenuous labor? I persevere only because the peace talks are not yet complete; I think to embody and carry out Your Majesty's instruction, to reform abuses and hopefully make lasting plans.
translations.idiomatic: He often told those close to him: "I am nearly eighty — how could I bear such strenuous labor? I persevere only because the peace talks are not yet complete; I mean to embody Your Majesty's instruction, reform abuses, and hopefully make plans that will endure.

sentences.zh: 儻初志略遂，即乞身而歸矣。」

translations.literal: If my initial resolve is in some measure fulfilled, I will immediately request my person and return home."
translations.idiomatic: If my initial resolve is in some measure fulfilled, I will immediately request leave and return home.

sentences.zh: 是年六月卒，年七十有八，贈資政殿學士、正奉大夫，諡「正惠」。

translations.literal: He died in the sixth month of that year, at age seventy-eight; he was posthumously granted Academician of the Zizheng Hall and Senior Grand Master of Positive Attendance; his posthumous title was Zhenghui ("Correct and Gracious").
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth month of that year, at the age of seventy-eight; he was posthumously granted Academician of the Zizheng Hall and Senior Grand Master of Positive Attendance, with the posthumous title Zhenghui ("Correct and Gracious").

sentences.zh: 大中清修寡欲，退然如不勝衣，及其遇事而發，凜乎不可犯。

translations.literal: Dazhong was pure in conduct and sparing in desire; withdrawn as if his clothes were too heavy for him — yet when affairs arose and he spoke out, he was imposing and not to be violated.
translations.idiomatic: Dazhong was pure in conduct and sparing in desire; withdrawn as if his clothes were too heavy for his frame — yet when affairs arose and he spoke out, he was imposing and not to be crossed.

sentences.zh: 自少力學，趣向不凡。

translations.literal: From youth he applied himself to learning; his orientation was extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he applied himself to learning, and his orientation was extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 所著有奏議、外制、文集三十卷。

translations.literal: His writings included Memorials, Outer Drafts, and a collected works in thirty juan.
translations.idiomatic: His writings included Memorials, Outer Drafts, and a collected works in thirty juan.

sentences.zh: 陳騤，字叔進，台州臨海人。

translations.literal: Chen Kui, courtesy name Shujin, was a native of Linhai in Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Kui, courtesy name Shujin, was a native of Linhai in Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 紹興二十四年，試春官第一，秦檜當國，以秦塤居其上。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Shaoxing, he placed first in the spring palace examination; Qin Hui was in power and had Qin Sun placed above him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year of Shaoxing, he placed first in the spring palace examination; Qin Hui was in power and had Qin Sun placed above him.

sentences.zh: 累官遷將作少監、守秘書少監兼太子諭德。

translations.literal: Through successive appointments he rose to Vice Director of Palace Construction and retained the post of Vice Director of the Secretariat while additionally serving as Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Through successive appointments he rose to Vice Director of Palace Construction and retained the post of Vice Director of the Secretariat while also serving as Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 太子尹臨安，騤謂：「儲宮下親細務，不得專於學，非所以毓德也。」

translations.literal: The heir apparent governed Lin'an; Kui said: "The crown prince personally descends to petty affairs and cannot devote himself solely to study — this is not the way to nurture virtue."
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent governed Lin'an; Kui said: "The crown prince personally attends to petty affairs and cannot devote himself solely to study — this is not the way to nurture virtue.

sentences.zh: 太子矍然，亟辭。

translations.literal: The heir apparent started in alarm and quickly declined the post.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent started in alarm and quickly declined the post.

sentences.zh: 崔淵以外戚張說進，除秘書郎兼金部郎，騤封還詞頭。

translations.literal: Cui Yuan, as a maternal relative, had Zhang Yue advanced; he was appointed as Secretariat Gentleman and concurrently Director of the Gold Bureau; Kui sealed and returned the draft edict.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuan, as a maternal relative, had Zhang Yue advanced; he was appointed Secretariat Gentleman and concurrently Director of the Gold Bureau; Kui sealed and returned the draft edict.

sentences.zh: 未幾，出知贛州，易秀州。

translations.literal: Before long he was sent out as prefect of Ganzhou, then transferred to Xiuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was sent out as prefect of Ganzhou, then transferred to Xiuzhou.

sentences.zh: 召還，首言：「陛下銳意圖治，群下急於自媒，爭獻強兵理財之計，及畀以職，報效蔑聞。

translations.literal: Recalled to court, he spoke first: "Your Majesty is keen to bring order to the realm; subordinates urgently promote themselves, competing to offer plans for strengthening the army and managing finances — yet once offices are given them, no results of service are heard.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he spoke first: "Your Majesty is keen to bring order to the realm; subordinates are eager to promote themselves, competing to offer plans for strengthening the army and managing finances — yet once offices are given them, no results of service are heard.

sentences.zh: 宜杜邪諂之路。」

translations.literal: One ought to block the path of heterodox flattery."
translations.idiomatic: We ought to block the path of heterodox flattery."

sentences.zh: 再歸故官，遷秘書監兼崇政殿說書。

translations.literal: He returned again to his former office and was promoted to Director of the Secretariat while additionally serving as Lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He returned again to his former office and was promoted to Director of the Secretariat while also serving as Lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 淳熙五年，試中書舍人兼侍講、同修國史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chunxi, he passed examination for Secretariat Drafter, additionally served as Lecturer-in-Waiting, and jointly compiled the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Chunxi, he passed examination for Secretariat Drafter, additionally served as Lecturer-in-Waiting, and jointly compiled the national history.

sentences.zh: 二年春，雷雪，詔陳時政得失，騤疏三十條，如宮闈之分不嚴，則權柄移；

translations.literal: In spring of the second year, there was thunder and snow; an edict ordered memorials on the gains and losses of current policy; Kui submitted thirty items in a memorial, such as: if distinctions within the inner palace are not strict, then authority shifts;
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the second year, there was thunder and snow; an edict ordered memorials on the gains and losses of current policy; Kui submitted thirty items in a memorial, such as: if distinctions within the inner palace are not strict, then authority shifts;

sentences.zh: 內謁之漸不杜，則明斷息；

translations.literal: if the gradual encroachment of inner access is not stopped, then clear judgment ceases;
translations.idiomatic: if the gradual encroachment of inner access is not stopped, then clear judgment ceases;

sentences.zh: 謀臺諫于當路，則私黨植；

translations.literal: if censorial remonstrance is plotted with those in power, then private factions take root;
translations.idiomatic: if censorial remonstrance is plotted with those in power, then private factions take root;

sentences.zh: 諮將帥于近習，則賄賂行；

translations.literal: if generals are consulted through close attendants, then bribery flourishes;
translations.idiomatic: if generals are consulted through close attendants, then bribery flourishes;

sentences.zh: 不求讜論，則過失彰；

translations.literal: if straightforward counsel is not sought, then faults become manifest;
translations.idiomatic: if straightforward counsel is not sought, then faults become manifest;

sentences.zh: 不謹舊章，則取捨錯；

translations.literal: if old statutes are not carefully observed, then choices of policy go wrong;
translations.idiomatic: if old statutes are not carefully observed, then choices of policy go wrong;

sentences.zh: 宴飲不時，則精神昏；

translations.literal: if feasting and drinking are untimely, then the spirit grows dull;
translations.idiomatic: if feasting and drinking are untimely, then the spirit grows dull;

sentences.zh: 賜予無節，則財用竭。

translations.literal: if grants and gifts are without restraint, then revenues are exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: if grants and gifts are without restraint, then revenues are exhausted.

sentences.zh: 皆切于時病。

translations.literal: All cut to the ailments of the age.
translations.idiomatic: All cut to the ailments of the age.

sentences.zh: 三年三月，權禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year, he served as acting Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the third year, he served as acting Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 六月，同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, he became Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, he became Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 四年二月，參知政事。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year, he became Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fourth year, he became Vice Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 光宗以疾不朝垂華宮，會慶節稱壽又不果往。

translations.literal: Emperor Guangzong, owing to illness, did not attend court at Chonghua Palace; when the festival of celebration arrived for offering birthday congratulations, he again failed to go.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangzong, owing to illness, did not attend court at Chonghua Palace; when the festival of celebration arrived for offering birthday congratulations, he again failed to go.

sentences.zh: 騤三入奏，廷臣上疏者以百數，上感悟，以冬至日朝重華。

translations.literal: Kui entered to memorialize three times; court officials who submitted memorials numbered in the hundreds; the emperor was moved to understanding and on the winter solstice paid court at Chonghua.
translations.idiomatic: Kui entered to memorialize three times; court officials who submitted memorials numbered in the hundreds; the emperor was moved to understanding and on the winter solstice paid court at Chonghua.

sentences.zh: 五年正月朔旦，稱壽于慈福宮。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, on the first day of the month, he offered birthday congratulations at the Cifu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifth year, on the first day of the month, he offered birthday congratulations at the Cifu Palace.

sentences.zh: 孝宗崩，光宗以疾未臨喪，騤請正儲位以安人心。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozong died. Emperor Guangzong, owing to illness, had not yet attended the mourning rites. Kui memorialized requesting that the succession be regularized to settle the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozong died, Emperor Guangzong, still ill, had not yet gone into mourning. Chen Kui memorialized that the heir should be formally established at once to reassure the realm.

sentences.zh: 七月，攝行三省事。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, he acted in the affairs of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he served as acting head of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 寧宗即位，知樞密院事兼參知政事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ningzong ascended the throne, [Kui] was made Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and concurrently Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: When Ningzong took the throne, Chen Kui was appointed Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Vice Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 趙汝愚為右丞相，騤素所不快，未嘗同堂語。

translations.literal: Zhao Ruyu served as Right Grand Councilor. Kui had long disliked him and never spoke together in the same hall.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ruyu was Right Grand Councilor, and Chen Kui had never gotten along with him—they never so much as exchanged words in the same hall.

sentences.zh: 汝愚擬除劉光祖侍御史，騤奏曰：「劉光祖舊與臣有隙，光祖入臺，臣請避之。」

translations.literal: Ruyu planned to appoint Liu Guangzu as Attending Censor. Kui memorialized, saying: "Liu Guangzu and I have an old enmity. If Guangzu enters the Censorate, I request to withdraw to avoid him."
translations.idiomatic: When Ruyu proposed appointing Liu Guangzu as Attending Censor, Chen Kui memorialized: "Liu Guangzu and I have old grievances. If he joins the Censorate, I must ask to step aside."

sentences.zh: 汝愚愕而止。

translations.literal: Ruyu was startled and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyu was taken aback and dropped the appointment.

sentences.zh: 時韓侂胄恃傳言之勞，潛竊國柄。

translations.literal: At this time Han Tuozhou relied on the merit of transmitting the edict and secretly usurped state power.
translations.idiomatic: Han Tuozhou, trading on his role in relaying the succession edict, was quietly seizing control of the government.

sentences.zh: 吏部侍郎彭龜年論侂胄將為國患，不報。

translations.literal: Ministry of Personnel Vice Minister Peng Guinian discoursed that Tuozhou would become a national calamity. [The court] gave no response.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Guinian, Vice Minister of Personnel, warned that Tuozhou would prove a disaster for the state, but the court never answered.

sentences.zh: 於是龜年、侂胄俱請祠，騤曰：「以閤門去經筵，何以示天下？」

translations.literal: Thereupon both Guinian and Tuozhou requested temple appointments. Kui said: "To remove the Director of the Gate of Reception from the Classics Lecture—how can this be shown to the realm?"
translations.idiomatic: Both Peng Guinian and Han Tuozhou then asked for honorary temple posts. Chen Kui objected: "If you remove the man at the Gate of Reception from the emperor's Classics Lecture, what message does that send the empire?"

sentences.zh: 龜年竟外補。

translations.literal: In the end Guinian was assigned outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Peng Guinian was posted outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 侂胄語人曰：「彭侍郎不貪好官，固也，元樞亦欲為好人耶？」

translations.literal: Tuozhou said to someone: "Vice Minister Peng does not covet a fine office—that much is certain. Does the Chief Administrator of Military Affairs also wish to play the good man?"
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou told others: "Vice Minister Peng may not crave a good post—that I grant. But does the Chief of Military Affairs also want to play the saint?"

sentences.zh: 遂以資政殿大學士與郡，辭，詔提舉洞霄宮。

translations.literal: Thereupon [Kui] was given the title Grand Academician of the Hall for Cultivating Governance and a prefecture. He declined. An edict [appointed him] Supervisor of the Dongxiao Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Kui was offered the title Grand Academician of the Hall for Cultivating Governance along with a prefectural post. He declined, and an edict instead made him Supervisor of the Dongxiao Palace.

sentences.zh: 慶元二年，知婺州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qingyuan, he was made Prefect of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1196 he was appointed prefect of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 告老，授觀文殿學士、提舉洞霄宮。

translations.literal: He requested retirement on account of age and was granted the title Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature and Supervisor of the Dongxiao Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He retired on grounds of age and received the titles Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature and Supervisor of the Dongxiao Palace.

sentences.zh: 嘉泰三年卒，年七十六。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiatai he died, aged seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1203, at the age of seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 贈少傅，諡「文簡」。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Tutor and given the posthumous name "Wen Jian" (Refined and Simple).
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Junior Tutor and given the posthumous title Wen Jian, "Refined and Simple."

sentences.zh: 黃黼，字元章，臨安餘杭人也。

translations.literal: Huang Pu, style name Yuanzhang, was a native of Yuhang in Lin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Pu, courtesy name Yuanzhang, was a native of Yuhang in Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 少游太學，第進士，累遷太常博士。

translations.literal: In youth he studied at the Imperial University, passed the jinshi examination, and was repeatedly promoted to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he studied at the Imperial University, passed the jinshi examination, and rose through the ranks to become an Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 輪對，言：「周以輔翼之臣出任方伯，漢以牧守之最擢拜公卿，唐不歷邊任，不拜宰相，本朝不為三司等屬，不除清望官。

translations.literal: At a rotating audience he said: "In Zhou, assisting ministers were sent out as regional lords. In Han, the finest governors and prefects were promoted to ministers and councilors. In Tang, those who had not served on the frontier were not appointed Grand Councilors. In our dynasty, those who have not been subordinates in the Three Offices and the like are not appointed to prestigious offices.
translations.idiomatic: At an imperial audience he argued: "The Zhou sent their most capable ministers out to govern the regions. The Han promoted their best prefects and governors to the highest offices. The Tang would not appoint a man Grand Councilor unless he had frontier experience. Our own dynasty likewise does not give prestigious posts to men who have never served in the Three Offices or comparable bureaus.

sentences.zh: 仁宗時，韓琦、范仲淹、龐籍皆嘗經略西事，久歷邊任，始除執政。

translations.literal: During Renzong's time, Han Qi, Fan Zhongyan, and Pang Ji had all once commanded western campaigns, long served on the frontier, and only then were appointed to executive positions.
translations.idiomatic: Under Renzong, Han Qi, Fan Zhongyan, and Pang Ji had all commanded campaigns on the western frontier and served long years in border posts before they were brought into the central government.

sentences.zh: 邊奏復警，范仲淹至再請行。

translations.literal: When border reports again brought alarms, Fan Zhongyan repeatedly requested to go.
translations.idiomatic: When fresh alarms came from the border, Fan Zhongyan asked again and again to take the field.

sentences.zh: 貝州之變，文彥博親自討賊。

translations.literal: At the Beizhou mutiny, Wen Yanbo personally led troops to suppress the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: During the Beizhou uprising, Wen Yanbo personally took command to put down the rebels.

sentences.zh: 乞于時望近臣中，擇才略謀慮可以任重致遠者，或畀上流，或委方面，習知邊防利害，地形險阨，中外軍民亦孚其恩信，熟其威名。

translations.literal: I beg that among eminent near ministers, those selected for talent, strategy, and deliberation who can bear heavy responsibility and achieve far-reaching goals—whether assigned to the upper Yangtze or entrusted with a regional command—may become familiar with frontier advantages and dangers, terrain and strategic passes, so that both civil and military, inland and border populations will trust in their grace and good faith and know their reputation for authority.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that from among the most respected ministers at court you choose men of talent, strategy, and judgment—men capable of bearing great responsibility and seeing far ahead—and assign them either to the upper Yangtze or to regional commands, so that they may learn the strengths and dangers of the frontier, the lay of passes and terrain, and so that soldiers and civilians alike may come to trust their integrity and respect their name.

sentences.zh: 天下無事則取風績顯著者不次除拜，以尊朝廷。

translations.literal: When the realm is at peace, those whose achievements and conduct are outstanding should be promoted without regard to seniority, to honor the court.
translations.idiomatic: In times of peace, promote men whose record stands out, regardless of seniority, and so lend dignity to the throne.

sentences.zh: 邊鄙有警，則任以重寄，俾制方面。

translations.literal: When the border regions have alarms, they should be entrusted with heavy responsibility and empowered to control the regions.
translations.idiomatic: When the frontier flares up, entrust them with real authority over the regions.

sentences.zh: 出將入相，何所不可。」

translations.literal: To go out as general and enter as councilor—what cannot be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Men who can lead armies in the field and govern at court—what office could they not fill?"

sentences.zh: 上嘉獎曰：「如卿言，可謂盡用人之道。」

translations.literal: The emperor praised him, saying: "As you say—it may be called fully exhausting the Way of employing men."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended him: "What you propose is nothing less than the full art of putting men to use."

sentences.zh: 行太常丞，進秘書郎、提舉江東常平茶鹽，召為戶部員外郎。

translations.literal: He served as Acting Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was promoted to Secretary Gentleman and Supervisor of Jiangdong Granaries, Tea, and Salt, and was summoned as Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Acting Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then rose to Secretary Gentleman and Supervisor of Jiangdong Granaries, Tea, and Salt, and was recalled to the capital as Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 尋除直秘閣、兩浙路轉運判官，進直龍圖閣，升副使，辭，改直顯謨閣。

translations.literal: Soon after he was appointed Directly at the Secretariat Pavilion and Transport Commissioner for the Two Zhe Circuits, promoted to Directly at the Dragon Diagram Pavilion and raised to Vice Commissioner. He declined and was changed to Directly at the Hall for Manifesting Splendor.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made a Direct Attendant at the Secretariat Pavilion and Transport Commissioner for the Two Zhe Circuits, then promoted to Direct Attendant at the Dragon Diagram Pavilion and Vice Commissioner—but declined that last promotion and accepted instead the post of Direct Attendant at the Hall for Manifesting Splendor.

sentences.zh: 浙東瀕海之田，以旱澇告，常平儲蓄不足，黼捐漕計貸之。

translations.literal: Coastal fields in eastern Zhe suffered reports of drought and flood, and Ever-Normal Granary reserves were insufficient. Pu donated from transport bureau funds to lend grain.
translations.idiomatic: Coastal farmland in eastern Zhe was ravaged by drought and flood, and the Ever-Normal Granaries could not meet the need. Huang Pu drew on transport funds to lend grain to the afflicted.

sentences.zh: 毗陵饑民取糠粃雜草根以充食，郡縣不以聞，黼取民食以進，乞捐僧牒、緡錢振濟，所全活甚眾。

translations.literal: In Piling starving people took bran and chaff mixed with grass roots for food. The prefecture and counties did not report it. Pu took the people's food and presented it [to the court], requesting donation of monk certificates and cash for relief. The number he saved was very great.
translations.idiomatic: In Piling, starving people were eating bran, chaff, and grass roots. The local officials said nothing. Huang Pu carried samples of what the people were eating to the court and asked that monk ordination certificates and cash be released for relief. He saved a great many lives.

sentences.zh: 除中書門下檢正諸房公事，守殿中侍御史兼侍講，遷侍御史，行起居郎兼權刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Rectifier of Miscellaneous Affairs for the Central Secretariat, held the post of Attending Palace Censor concurrent with Lecturer, was transferred to Censor, and served as Acting Recorder and concurrent Acting Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Rectifier of Miscellaneous Affairs for the Central Secretariat, served as Attending Palace Censor while also lecturing the emperor, was promoted to Censor, and then acted as Recorder while concurrently holding the post of Acting Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 以劉德秀論劾，奉祠而卒。

translations.literal: Due to Liu Dexiu's impeachment memorial, he was granted a temple appointment and died.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Dexiu impeached him, he was given a temple post and died soon after.

sentences.zh: 詹體仁

translations.literal: Zhan Tiren
translations.idiomatic: Zhan Tiren

sentences.zh: 光宗即位，提舉浙西常平，除戶部員外郎、湖廣總領，就升司農少卿。

translations.literal: When Guangzong ascended the throne, [Tiren] was made Supervisor of Zhexi Ever-Normal Granaries, appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue and General Fiscal Supervisor for Huguang, and on the spot promoted to Vice Director of the Court of the National Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangzong took the throne, Zhan Tiren was put in charge of Zhexi Ever-Normal Granaries, then appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue and General Fiscal Supervisor for Huguang, and immediately promoted to Vice Director of the Court of the National Granaries.

sentences.zh: 奏蠲諸郡賦輸積欠百餘萬。

translations.literal: He memorialized remitting over a million in accumulated arrears of tax deliveries from various prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized remission of more than a million in accumulated tax arrears owed by the prefectures.

sentences.zh: 有逃卒千人入大冶，因鐵鑄錢，剽掠為變。

translations.literal: A thousand deserting soldiers entered Daye and, through iron-casting coin operations, plundered and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand deserters entered Daye, seized the iron foundries used for coining, and turned to plunder and rebellion.

sentences.zh: 體仁語戎帥：「此去京師千餘里，若比上請得報，賊勢張矣。

translations.literal: Tiren told the military commander: "This place is over a thousand li from the capital. If we wait to request approval from above before acting, the bandits' power will have swelled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan Tiren told the regional commander: "We are more than a thousand li from the capital. If we wait for approval from court, the rebels will have grown beyond control.

sentences.zh: 宜速加誅討。」

translations.literal: We should speedily add extermination and suppression."
translations.idiomatic: We must strike at once."

sentences.zh: 帥用其言，群黨悉散。

translations.literal: The commander adopted his advice, and the whole band dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: The commander followed his counsel, and the rebel band broke up completely.

sentences.zh: 除太常少卿，陛對，首陳父子至恩之說，謂：「《易》于《家人》之後次之以《睽》，《睽》之上九曰：『見豕負塗，載鬼一車，先張之弧，後說之弧，匪寇婚媾，往，遇雨則吉。』

translations.literal: Appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. At audience before the throne, he first presented the doctrine of the utmost bond between father and son, saying: "The Classic of Changes, after the Family, next places Separation. The top line of Separation says: 'He sees a pig smeared with mud, a cartload of ghosts; he first draws his bow, then he unstrings his bow—it is not raiders but a bridal party; going forth, if he meets rain, then it is auspicious.'
translations.idiomatic: Appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, he addressed the throne and opened with the doctrine of the deepest bond between father and son. He cited the Classic of Changes: after the hexagram Family comes Separation, whose top line reads, "He sees a pig smeared with mud, a cartload of ghosts. He first draws his bow, then unstrings it—not raiders but a wedding party. Go forward: meeting rain brings good fortune.

sentences.zh: 夫疑極而惑，凡所見者皆以為寇，而不知實其親也。

translations.literal: When suspicion reaches its extreme and one is confused, everything one sees is taken for raiders, yet one does not know it is actually one's kin.
translations.idiomatic: When suspicion runs to its extreme, everything looks like an enemy—even what is in truth one's own kin.

sentences.zh: 孔子釋之曰：『遇雨則吉，群疑亡也』。

translations.literal: Confucius explained it, saying: "To meet rain is auspicious—the multitude of doubts are extinguished."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius glossed the line: "Meeting rain is auspicious—all doubts are dispelled."

sentences.zh: 蓋人倫天理，有間隔而無斷絕，方其未通也，湮鬱煩憒，若不可以終日；

translations.literal: For human relations and Heaven's principle, there is estrangement but no severance. When it has not yet been connected, depression and vexation are oppressive, as if one cannot endure a single day;
translations.idiomatic: Human bonds ordained by Heaven may be strained, yet they are never truly severed. While the rift remains, grief and turmoil weigh on the heart as if the day itself cannot be endured;

sentences.zh: 及其醒然而悟，泮然而釋，如遇雨焉，何其和悅而條暢也。

translations.literal: and when one awakens to clarity and releases with melting ease, it is like meeting rain—how harmonious and unimpeded!
translations.idiomatic: but once understanding dawns and the heart melts open, it is like rain falling on parched ground—suddenly harmonious, clear, and at ease.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下神心昭融，聖度恢豁，凡厥疑情，一朝渙然若揭日月而開雲霧。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Majesty's divine mind is luminous and harmonized, your sagely breadth is expansive and open; all such doubting sentiments will in one morning dissolve like lifting sun and moon and parting clouds and mist.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's mind is luminous, your magnanimity boundless. Let every lingering doubt dissolve in a single morning, as sun and moon break through cloud and mist.

sentences.zh: 丕敘彝倫，以承兩宮之歡，以塞兆民之望。」

translations.literal: Greatly regulate the constant human relations, thereby to inherit the joy of the Two Palaces and to fulfill the hopes of the myriad people."
translations.idiomatic: Restore the right order among kin, bring joy to both palaces, and answer the hopes of the people."

sentences.zh: 時上以積疑成疾，久不過重華宮，故體仁引《易》睽弧之義，以開廣聖意。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor had formed illness from accumulated suspicion and long had not visited Chonghua Palace; therefore Tiren cited the meaning of Separation and the bow in the Changes to broaden the sage intent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had fallen ill from long-nurtured suspicion and had not visited Chonghua Palace in some time. Tiren invoked this passage from Separation to open a path back to reconciliation.

sentences.zh: 孝宗崩，體仁率同列抗疏，請駕詣重華宮親臨祥祭，辭意懇切。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong died, Tiren led his colleagues in a direct memorial requesting the imperial carriage proceed to Chonghua Palace to personally attend the auspicious mourning rites. His language was earnest and pressing.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong died, Zhan Tiren led his colleagues in a direct memorial urging the emperor to go in person to Chonghua Palace for the mourning rites. His words were urgent and heartfelt.

sentences.zh: 時趙汝愚將定大策，外庭無預謀者，密令體仁及左司郎官徐誼達意少保吳琚，請憲聖太后垂簾為援立計。

translations.literal: At the time Zhao Ruyu was about to fix the great plan. None outside the inner court were privy to the plotting. He secretly ordered Tiren and Left Directorate Gentleman Xu Yi to convey his intent to Junior Tutor Wu Ju, requesting Empress Dowager Xiansheng preside from behind the curtain to support the enthronement plan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ruyu was then preparing a decisive move, and no one outside the inner court knew of it. He secretly sent Tiren and Left Directorate Gentleman Xu Yi to Junior Tutor Wu Ju with a message asking Empress Dowager Xiansheng to preside from behind the curtain and support the plan to install a new emperor.

sentences.zh: 寧宗登極，天下晏然，體仁與諸賢密贊汝愚之力也。

translations.literal: When Ningzong ascended the imperial position, the realm was tranquil. Tiren and the worthy men secretly assisted Ruyu's power.
translations.idiomatic: When Ningzong took the throne, the realm settled peacefully—thanks in no small part to the quiet support Zhan Tiren and other worthy men gave Zhao Ruyu.

sentences.zh: 時議大行皇帝諡，體仁言：「壽皇聖帝事德壽二十餘年，極天下之養，諒陰三年，不御常服，漢、唐以來未之有，宜諡曰『孝』。」

translations.literal: At the time there was discussion of the late emperor's posthumous title. Tiren said: "Emperor Shouhuang served at Dezhao for more than twenty years, providing the utmost nurturing in the realm. For three years in mourning garments he wore no ordinary dress—since Han and Tang there has been nothing like it. The posthumous name should be 'Xiao' (Filial)."
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated the posthumous title of the late emperor, Tiren argued: "For more than twenty years Emperor Shouhuang attended his father at the Dezhao Palace with every honor filial devotion could offer. For three years of mourning he wore no ordinary dress—a feat unmatched since Han and Tang. His posthumous name should be Xiao, 'Filial.'"

sentences.zh: 卒用其言。

translations.literal: In the end his words were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The court accepted his recommendation.

sentences.zh: 孝宗將復土，體仁言：「永阜陵地勢卑下，非所以妥安神靈。」

translations.literal: When Xiaozong was about to be reburied, Tiren said: "The terrain of Yongfu Mausoleum is low and inferior—it is not what can properly settle the spirit."
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong's remains were to be reinterred, Tiren objected: "The ground at Yongfu Mausoleum is too low and poor—it is no fit resting place for an emperor's spirit."

sentences.zh: 與宰相異議，除太府卿。

translations.literal: Disagreeing with the Grand Councilor, he was appointed Director of the Imperial Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: He broke with the chief minister on the matter and was transferred to the post of Director of the Imperial Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 尋直龍圖閣、知福州，言者竟以前論山陵事罷之。

translations.literal: Soon after he was Directly at the Dragon Diagram Pavilion and Prefect of Fuzhou. Memorializers eventually had him dismissed on account of his earlier discussion of the imperial tomb.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Direct Attendant at the Dragon Diagram Pavilion and prefect of Fuzhou, but critics eventually forced his removal over his earlier objections to the tomb site.

sentences.zh: 退居霅川，日以經史自娛，人莫窺其際。

translations.literal: He retired to live at Zhaichuan, spending his days with the Classics and histories for pleasure. No one could fathom his inner state.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew to Zhaichuan and passed his days reading the Classics and histories. No one could tell what he truly thought.

sentences.zh: 始，體仁使浙右，時蘇師旦以胥吏執役，後倚侂胄躐躋大官，至是遣介通殷勤。

translations.literal: Initially, when Tiren served in western Zhe, Su Shidan at the time was a clerk performing corvée duty. Later, relying on Tuozhou, he leaped to high office. At this time he sent an intermediary with warm attentions.
translations.idiomatic: When Tiren had earlier served in western Zhe, Su Shidan was no more than a clerk on corvée duty. Later, backed by Han Tuozhou, he vaulted into high office. Now he sent an emissary with cordial overtures.

sentences.zh: 體仁曰：「小人乘君子之器，禍至無日矣，烏得以汙我！」

translations.literal: Tiren said: "A petty man occupying a gentleman's vessel—disaster will come any day now. How could I let myself be polluted by him!"
translations.idiomatic: Tiren replied: "When a petty man seizes a gentleman's place, ruin follows soon enough. I will not let him stain me."

sentences.zh: 未幾，果敗。

translations.literal: Before long, [Shidan] indeed fell.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Su Shidan did indeed fall.

sentences.zh: 復直龍圖閣、知靜江府，閣十縣稅錢一萬四千，蠲雜賦八千。

translations.literal: Again Directly at the Dragon Diagram Pavilion and Prefect of Jingjiang Prefecture. He reduced ten counties' tax cash by fourteen thousand and remitted miscellaneous levies of eight thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Direct Attendant at the Dragon Diagram Pavilion and prefect of Jingjiang, where he cut tax payments by fourteen thousand cash across ten counties and remitted eight thousand in miscellaneous levies.

sentences.zh: 移守鄂州，除司農卿，復總湖廣餉事。

translations.literal: Transferred to govern E Prefecture, appointed Director of the Court of the National Granaries, again supervising Huguang provisions.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to E Prefecture, appointed Director of the Court of the National Granaries, and again put in charge of supplies for Huguang.

sentences.zh: 時歲凶艱食，即以便宜發廩振捄而後以聞。

translations.literal: At the time the year was bad and food was scarce. He immediately on emergency authority opened granaries for relief and only afterward reported.
translations.idiomatic: That year harvests failed and food grew scarce. He opened the granaries on his own emergency authority and reported to court afterward.

sentences.zh: 侂胄建議開邊，一時爭談兵以規進用。

translations.literal: Tuozhou proposed opening the border [to war]. For a time all competed to talk of military affairs to seek advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Han Tuozhou urged opening hostilities on the frontier, and for a time officials vied to talk up war in hopes of promotion.

sentences.zh: 體仁移書廟堂，言兵不可輕動，宜遵養俟時。

translations.literal: Tiren wrote to the court, saying troops must not be lightly moved; one should follow nurturing and await the proper time.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren wrote to the central government warning that war must not be lightly undertaken and urging patience until the moment was right.

sentences.zh: 皇甫斌自以將家子，好言兵，體仁語僚屬，謂斌必敗，已而果然。

translations.literal: Huangfu Bin, considering himself the son of a military family, loved to speak of war. Tiren told his staff that Bin would surely fail—and before long it was indeed so.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Bin, proud of his family's military pedigree, was eager to talk of war. Tiren told his staff that Bin was bound to fail—and so he did, before long.

sentences.zh: 開禧二年卒，年六十四。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaixi he died, aged sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1206, at the age of sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 體仁穎邁特立，博極群書。

translations.literal: Tiren was sharp, lofty, and independent; he had exhaustively read all books.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren was brilliant, upright, and independent, and had read widely across every field of learning.

sentences.zh: 少從朱熹學，以存誠慎獨為主。

translations.literal: In youth he studied under Zhu Xi, taking preservation of sincerity and careful solitude as his foundation.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he studied under Zhu Xi and made sincerity and moral vigilance in solitude the foundation of his life.

sentences.zh: 為文明暢，悉根諸理。

translations.literal: His literary compositions were clear and fluent, all rooted in principle.
translations.idiomatic: His writing was lucid and graceful, always grounded in principle.

sentences.zh: 周必大當國，體仁嘗疏薦三十餘人，皆當世知名士。

translations.literal: When Zhou Bidá held power, Tiren once memorialized recommending more than thirty men—all renowned scholars of the age.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhou Bidá was chief minister, Tiren once recommended more than thirty men by memorial—all distinguished figures of the day.

sentences.zh: 郡人真德秀早從其遊，嘗問居官蒞民之法，體仁曰：「盡心、平心而已，盡心則無愧，平心則無偏。」

translations.literal: His fellow townsman Zhen Dexiu in youth followed him in study and once asked about the method of holding office and governing the people. Tiren said: "Exhaust the heart and level the heart—that is all. Exhaust the heart and there is no shame; level the heart and there is no partiality."
translations.idiomatic: His townsman Zhen Dexiu studied with him from an early age and once asked how to govern well. Tiren answered: "Give your whole heart and keep an even heart—that is all. Give your whole heart and you will have no regrets; keep an even heart and you will show no favoritism."

sentences.zh: 世服其確論云。

translations.literal: The world admired his definitive judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Later generations admired the soundness of his counsel.

sentences.zh: 論曰：彭龜年、黃裳、羅點以青宮師保之舊，盡言無隱。

translations.literal: The commentators say: Peng Guinian, Huang Shang, and Luo Dian, by virtue of their old ties as tutors and protectors of the Eastern Palace, spoke fully without concealment.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators observe: Peng Guinian, Huang Shang, and Luo Dian, having once served as tutors to the crown prince, spoke their minds without reserve.

sentences.zh: 黃度、林大中亦能守正不阿，進退裕如。

translations.literal: Huang Du and Lin Dazhong also could uphold rectitude without compromise, advancing and withdrawing with ease.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Du and Lin Dazhong likewise held to principle without bending, and moved through office and retirement with equal grace.

sentences.zh: 此數臣者，皆能推明所學，務引君以當道，可謂粹然君子矣。

translations.literal: These several ministers all could extend and clarify what they had learned, striving to lead the ruler onto the proper Way—they may be called pure gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: These men applied what they had learned in earnest, each striving to guide the ruler toward the right path. They were gentlemen in the truest sense.

sentences.zh: 陳騤論事頗切時病，詹體仁深于理學，皆有足稱者。

translations.literal: Chen Kui in discussing affairs was quite cutting toward the ills of the times. Zhan Tiren was deep in Neo-Confucian learning. Both have points worth praising.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Kui's memorials cut sharply to the problems of the day, and Zhan Tiren was deeply versed in Neo-Confucian learning. Both deserve recognition.

sentences.zh: 然騤嘗詆譏呂祖謙，至視趙汝愚、劉光祖為仇，而體仁乃能以朱熹、真德秀為師友，即其所好惡，而二人之邪正，於是可知焉。

translations.literal: Yet Kui once reviled and ridiculed Lü Zuqian, going so far as to treat Zhao Ruyu and Liu Guangzu as enemies, while Tiren was able to take Zhu Xi and Zhen Dexiu as teacher and friends. From what they each favored and hated, the rectitude and depravity of the two men can thus be known.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Chen Kui reviled Lü Zuqian and treated Zhao Ruyu and Liu Guangzu as enemies, whereas Tiren counted Zhu Xi and Zhen Dexiu among his teachers and friends. From what each man loved and hated, the moral quality of the two becomes plain.
